research.summary:
What the evidence says. Boeing is tied to Washington more closely than almost any other US company. US government contracts provided 35-51% of its revenue in 2020-2025 (51% in 2020, 42% in 2024, 35% in 2025). It won both US sixth-generation fighter awards (F-47 in March 2025, F/A-XX in September 2026). Presidential trade deals brought it orders: Boeing and GE together made up $215B of the $244B in foreign contracts that Commerce helped win in 2025, and a May 2026 Trump-Xi summit produced a 200-jet China commitment that, in Ortberg's words, reopened China "to our narrowbody airplanes". DOJ settled the 737 MAX criminal case with a non-prosecution agreement, and the case was dismissed in November 2025. The FAA controls the 737 rate cap, which has gone from 38 to 42 to 47 a month. Boeing claims about 1.5 million supported US jobs and Commerce claims 1.8 million; Commerce also cites $43B a year of US supplier spend. These are multiplier estimates, not headcount; the IAM 751 machinists alone number 30,000-34,000. Since 2025 Washington has also shown it will take equity in strategic firms (Intel 9.9%, MP Materials 15%, a golden share in US Steel), and in August 2025 Commerce Secretary Lutnick named Boeing among defense firms where stakes were being discussed. So the user is right that exit would carry political weight.

Boeing's record shows a different pattern, though. Political and jobs pressure has mostly decided where Boeing builds and on what terms, not whether it builds. Boeing:
- ignored Washington state's governors (787 line to South Carolina in 2009 and all 787 production there in 2020; about 300 engineering jobs moving there in 2026);
- cut about 10,000 jobs in 2009, about 26,000 in 2020 and about 17,000 in 2024;
- turned down CARES Act loans, which came with possible equity strings, and raised $25B in bonds instead (2020);
- paused the NASA co-funded X-66 demonstrator in 2025;
- ended the 757 in 2004, the 747 in 2023 and the 767 freighter (2027), with no visible penalty from Washington.

Pressure did change two kinds of decision. On safety, Boeing withdrew its MAX 7 exemption request under Senate pressure in 2024. On terms, Boeing used site choice to win incentives: $8.7B from Washington in 2013, $450-900M from South Carolina in 2009 plus $120M in 2025, and $155M from St. Louis County. I found no statement by a US official or member of Congress demanding a 737 successor or warning against leaving narrowbodies to Airbus or COMAC. The national-security argument so far comes from think tanks (ITIF, June 2026) and from Boeing calling itself a top US exporter. In March 2026 the CFO said a new programme will come but is "not any time near".

How this could move the fps decision (my inferences, not sourced estimates):
1. The cash channels are real but limited. An auction of the final-assembly site could plausibly yield incentives worth about $1-3B in present value. NASA or DoD co-funding of technology (the X-66 precedent was $425M) would add less than $1B. Government sales help raises order capture. Together this is about the size of the Board's $2B H8 doctrine-premium cap. That can decide ties or the 8.1% case, but cannot close a $4-9B gap at 10.5% on its own. The 2024 IAM contract ties any launch before about 2028 to Puget Sound, which removes the site auction.
2. Downside risk. Washington's willingness to rescue a national champion (the $17B CARES set-aside, the lenient DOJ deal, the equity stakes) acts like an implicit safety net under the -$1B downside test. Boeing itself has avoided taking government equity.
3. Leverage. Washington can reward or punish Boeing through defense awards, FAA rate approvals and trade deals. I found no case where it punished Boeing for a commercial product choice; the 2025-26 defense awards look merit-based.
4. Timing. Under Do Nothing the exit falls in 2045-2060, so the political cost lands decades out. Airbus already builds A320s in Mobile, Alabama (two A320 lines plus an A220 line, more than 2,000 staff), which weakens the "all the jobs leave the US" argument.

Suggestion: model Washington and brand value as a capped premium with stated sources (for example $1-3B), plus a scenario in which Washington offers launch support with conditions, rather than as an open-ended override.

Access note: WebFetch could not reach trade.gov, boeing.com or sec.gov, so web findings rely on search-result excerpts. The repo transcripts and the FY2008-FY2024 10-Ks were read directly from the PDFs (page numbers below are PDF pages of 'Transcripts from 2006-2025_Compressed.pdf', 'Boeing 10ks.pdf' and 'Transcript Digest (4).pdf').

findings.topic: Jobs: Boeing workforce size and location
findings.claim: Boeing employed about 172,000 people at end-2024, 15% outside the US (about 146,000 in the US; about 58,000 union members). At end-2025 it had just under 182,000. Washington state fell by more than 2,500 to 65,024 and South Carolina grew about 10% to 9,059.
findings.source: Boeing 10-K FY2024, 'Boeing 10ks.pdf' p.2166 (repo; B-2239 cites the same page). State split from Everett Herald / Post and Courier reporting, Feb 2026, seen only in search excerpts: https://www.heraldnet.com/business/state-share-of-boeing-jobs-grows-even-as-number-shrinks ; https://www.postandcourier.com/business/aerospace/boeing-sc-hired-workers-payroll-2025/article_356964af-461f-4b8d-aeb1-6c309c94824b.html
findings.quote: As of December 31, 2024, Boeing's total workforce was approximately 172,000 with 15% located outside of the U.S.
findings.use_in_model: Sets the size of the jobs at stake. Do Nothing phases out the MAX in 2045-2060, so the exposed jobs are future jobs and no near-term layoff is triggered. Any political penalty should be discounted to that date.

findings.topic: Jobs: IAM 751 and the 2024 strike
findings.claim: IAM 751 represents more than 30,000 Boeing manufacturing workers, mostly in Washington, where the 737 is built (Renton). In September 2024, 96% voted to strike. About 33,000 struck for 53 days and settled on 4 Nov 2024 (59% yes): 38% raises over four years, pension not restored. Boeing paused all commercial production except the non-union Charleston 787 line. Commercial Airplanes' Q3 2024 operating margin was -54%. Anderson Economic Group estimated combined losses of $7.6B by late October and more than $9.6B by week six. By April 2026 the union factory workforce in the Pacific Northwest exceeded 34,000, with Boeing hiring 100-140 a week.
findings.source: 10-K FY2024 p.2173 (B-2240) and p.2166 (B-2239); FQ3 2024 call p.138 (B-2213); Anderson Economic Group https://www.andersoneconomicgroup.com/boeing-strike-weekly-economic-loss-estimates/ ; Fox Business https://foxbusiness.com/economy/boeing-strike-costliest-economic-damage-2024-so-far ; Al Jazeera 2024-11-01 https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/11/1/boeing-workers-to-vote-on-38-pay-rise-offer-to-end-weeks-long-strike ; Reuters via MarketScreener, 16 Apr 2026 https://www.marketscreener.com/news/boeing-hiring-more-than-100-factory-workers-a-week-to-grow-output-replace-retirees-ce7e50dddc88f222
findings.quote: our contract with IAM 751, which represents over 30,000 Boeing manufacturing employees primarily located in Washington state, expired and 96% of IAM 751 members voted to initiate a strike.
findings.use_in_model: The union has real leverage and strikes are costly. Boeing's CFO sized the settlement at less than 5% of airplane cost (B-2223). The political weight of these workers sits mainly with the Washington delegation, not nationally.

findings.topic: Jobs: 2024 IAM clause on the next new airplane
findings.claim: The 2024 IAM contract commits Boeing to build its next new airplane, including initial and derivative models, in Puget Sound. The commitment applies only if the Board approves a launch during the four-year term (to about 2028). Boeing's Stephanie Pope presented it as Puget Sound building Boeing's next new airplane.
findings.source: FlightGlobal, Sept 2024: https://www.flightglobal.com/airframers/boeing-and-machinists-union-reach-tentative-contract-deal-ahead-of-12-september-member-vote/159889.article ; Everett Herald 2024-09-08: https://www.heraldnet.com/2024/09/08/boeing-reaches-tentative-pact-with-machinists/ (search excerpts; contract text not seen)
findings.quote: a commitment by Boeing to build its next new aircraft in the Puget Sound region – but only if Boeing's board of directors approves the launch of an aircraft during the four-year contract's term
findings.use_in_model: A launch before about 2028 is tied to unionised Puget Sound, so Boeing cannot auction the site for state incentives. A later launch keeps the auction open. It also shows Washington state politics already expects a new airplane.

findings.topic: Jobs: Boeing and government jobs claims
findings.claim: Boeing and the US government regularly put numbers on Boeing-supported US jobs. Boeing (Jan 2017) said more than 13,000 US supplier companies sustain about 1.5 million aerospace jobs; in July 2020 it cited more than 12,000 suppliers and about 1.5 million jobs. Commerce (Sept 2025) said Boeing directly and indirectly supports 1.8 million US jobs and spends $43B a year with US suppliers in every state. Commerce also gives job counts per deal: 123,000 for the Turkish 787 order and 101,000 for the 737 MAX order. These are multiplier estimates, not headcount.
findings.source: Transcripts 2006-2025 PDF p.1521 (FQ4 2016 call, 25 Jan 2017; Muilenburg) and p.836 (FQ2 2020 call, 29 Jul 2020); Commerce ITA press release Sept 2025, https://www.trade.gov/press-release/commerce-champions-us-jobs-landmark-boeing-turkish-airlines-deal (fetch blocked; search excerpt)
findings.quote: we and our supply chain of more than 13,000 companies in the United States create and sustain about 1.5 million aerospace jobs
findings.use_in_model: This is the figure politicians will cite for an exit. The 737 made up 440 of Boeing's 600 deliveries in 2025 (The National, 13 Jan 2026), so by inference a large share of the claimed jobs rides on the narrowbody. Treat it as political salience, not cash.

findings.topic: Past behaviour: protecting the 737 ecosystem during the grounding
findings.claim: In 2019 Boeing resisted shutting MAX production, citing more than 600 suppliers and hundreds of thousands of jobs. It then kept the 737 workforce and infrastructure through the 2020 production suspension, absorbing about $4B of abnormal costs, and avoided layoffs until COVID.
findings.source: Transcripts 2006-2025 PDF p.965 (conference, 7 Aug 2019; B-1584); p.898 (FQ4 2019 call, 29 Jan 2020; B-1618); p.858 (FQ1 2020 call; B-1672)
findings.quote: If you think about our production line against 600-some suppliers, hundreds of thousands of jobs that would be impacted, and we're very mindful about supply chain health
findings.unit: USD billion abnormal costs accepted to keep the 737 workforce
findings.use_in_model: Boeing has paid billions to keep its narrowbody workforce and suppliers together. That supports counting lost ecosystem value (stranded overhead, supplier health) against Do Nothing. But this was a temporary halt, not a permanent exit.

findings.topic: Counter-evidence: large job cuts despite political sensitivity
findings.claim: Boeing cut about 10,000 jobs in 2009 and recorded severance for about 26,000 in 2020, targeting a 130,000 workforce. In October 2024 it announced about 17,000 cuts (10%), which Ortberg attributed to overstaffing rather than the strike. Of the first 5,080 positions identified, about 2,600 were in Washington. Boeing then rehired about 23,000 a year in 2022 and 2023.
findings.source: Transcripts p.2848 (B-0147); 10-K FY2020 p.1361 (B-1767); FQ3 2020 call p.799 (BX-0229); FQ3 2024 call p.143 (B-2206); Spokesman-Review 2024-10-11 https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/oct/11/boeing-will-shed-17000-jobs-as-financial-woes-deep/ ; 10-K FY2022/FY2023 (B-1997, B-2105)
findings.quote: During 2020, we recorded severance costs for approximately 26,000 employees
findings.use_in_model: Weighs against a large jobs penalty on Do Nothing. Boeing has shed tens of thousands of jobs whenever finances required, with no measurable retaliation from Washington.

findings.topic: Past behaviour: 787 second line in South Carolina and the NLRB case (2009-2011)
findings.claim: Boeing put the second 787 final-assembly line in non-union North Charleston, partly to diversify its labour base after the 2008 strike. South Carolina offered an incentive package first valued at $450M (3,800 jobs, $750M investment), later estimated above $900M. The NLRB General Counsel issued a retaliation complaint in April 2011. It was withdrawn on 9 Dec 2011 after the IAM signed a four-year extension. Boeing never reversed the siting.
findings.source: FQ3 2009 call p.2792 (B-0218); 10-K FY2009 p.1730 (B-0254); HuffPost https://www.huffpost.com/entry/boeing-complaint-dropped-nlrb_n_1139139 ; Everett Herald https://www.heraldnet.com/business/nlrb-drops-complaint-against-boeing-2/ ; incentives: https://www.aviationpros.com/home/news/10380994/south-carolina-lands-boeing ; https://www.heraldnet.com/business/boeing-got-more-than-900-million-in-incentives-from-s-c-report/
findings.quote: diversifying our labor pool and labor relationship has some benefits ... I've got to figure out a way to reduce that risk to the company. (McNerney)
findings.use_in_model: Counter-evidence. Federal and home-state pressure did not change the site; it was settled through a union contract. It also shows states will pay hundreds of millions for a final-assembly line, a lever that lowers fps cost.

findings.topic: Past behaviour: 777X siting and Washington's 2013 tax package
findings.claim: In a November 2013 special session Washington extended aerospace tax breaks to 2040, valued at $8.7B (Senate 42-2, House 75-11). Machinists rejected Boeing's first offer, then approved a pension freeze and extension to 2024 by 51% in January 2014. Boeing reported $305M of state tax savings in 2015 and $242M in 2016. Its Washington headcount fell about 16,700 between 2012 and 2018, roughly half after the extension. A state audit found no causal link between the breaks and jobs, and bills to tie the breaks to job levels failed.
findings.source: FQ4 2013 call p.2030 (B-0849); 10-K FY2013 p.2759 (B-0881); Reuters via Yahoo https://finance.yahoo.com/news/washington-state-senate-passes-tax-breaks-aiming-win-222147729--finance.html ; Herald https://www.heraldnet.com/news/boeing-says-it-saved-305m-through-state-tax-breaks-in-2015/ ; https://www.heraldnet.com/news/boeings-washington-tax-break-savings-in-2016-242-million ; https://www.heraldnet.com/news/unions-blast-boeing-for-paring-jobs-since-2013-tax-break-extension (search excerpts)
findings.quote: This solidifies production for the 777X in the Puget Sound region (McNerney, Jan 2014)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing can turn political pressure into cash by auctioning a new programme's site. My inference: a comparable package for the fps could be worth about $1.5-3B PV at 10.5%, but only outside the 2024 IAM clause window. Jobs pledges attached to such packages have not held.

findings.topic: Counter-evidence: Washington's 2020 tax repeal and 787 consolidation
findings.claim: In February 2020 Boeing asked Washington to suspend its preferential B&O tax rate to resolve the WTO case; lawmakers repealed it in March 2020, with a snapback clause. On 1 Oct 2020 Boeing moved all 787 production to South Carolina and closed the Everett line. Governor Inslee called it 'an insult' and ordered a review of roughly $100M a year in tax benefits. In February 2026 Boeing began moving about 300 787 engineering jobs to South Carolina. In November 2025 it broke ground on a $1B South Carolina expansion backed by $120M in state bonds.
findings.source: Fortune 2020-02-20 https://fortune.com/2020/02/20/boeing-preferential-tax-rate-wto ; NW News Network 2020-03-12 https://www.nwnewsnetwork.org/government-and-politics/2020-03-12/boeing-asked-washington-state-lawmakers-to-raise-its-taxes-they-did ; Herald 2020-10-01 https://www.heraldnet.com/2020/10/01/boeing-to-move-787-production-to-south-carolina-by-mid-2021/ ; Leeham 2020-10-01 https://leehamnews.com/2020/10/01/boeing-needs-to-show-respect-for-taxpayers-gov-inslee-says/ ; Spokesman 2026-02-05 https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/feb/05/boeing-moves-more-787-work-from-washington ; https://www.plantservices.com/industry-news/news/55261904/boeing-invests-1b-to-upgrade-south-carolina-facilities-creating-500-new-jobs
findings.quote: When the market comes back, so should these jobs. (Inslee, Oct 2020)
findings.number: ~100M/yr tax benefit; 300 engineering jobs; $1B SC capex; $120M SC bonds
findings.use_in_model: Pressure from home-state governors has been cheap for Boeing to ignore. Do not give state politics much weight on whether to launch; it matters for where and on what terms.

findings.topic: Past behaviour: headquarters moves toward Washington, DC
findings.claim: Boeing moved its headquarters from Seattle to Chicago in 2001, with about $60M of incentives over 20 years, to separate the head office from the business units. In May 2022 it moved to Arlington, Virginia, citing proximity to customers and stakeholders; Reuters read this as reflecting its dependence on the federal government. No large incentive package was involved. Rep. DeFazio criticised the move.
findings.source: CNN Money 2001-05-10 https://money.cnn.com/2001/05/10/companies/boeing/ ; CNBC 2022-05-05 https://www.cnbc.com/2022/05/05/boeing-to-move-headquarters-from-chicago-to-virginia-.html ; NBC Washington 2022 (search excerpts)
findings.quote: The region makes strategic sense for our global headquarters given its proximity to our customers and stakeholders (Calhoun)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing organises its corporate centre around Washington, so it is exposed to the capital's view of a narrowbody exit. The move itself shows no willingness to pay for national-champion status.

findings.topic: Counter-evidence: Boeing has left segments before (757, 747, 767F)
findings.claim: Boeing ended the 757 in October 2004 after 1,050 built, with no replacement; it said newer 737s and the 787 would cover the market, and the Airbus A321 took the segment. The last 747 was delivered on 31 Jan 2023 after 1,574 built over 54 years. In 2024 Boeing decided to end the 767 freighter in 2027, taking $580M of reach-forward losses. I found no visible political penalty for any of these exits.
findings.source: InsideFlyer https://www.insideflyer.com/posts/boeings-757-cancellation-leaves-gap-in-narrowbody-market/ ; AvWeb https://avweb.com/aviation-news/last-boeing-747-delivered ; 10-K FY2024 p.2201 (B-2246)
findings.quote: During the third quarter of 2024, we decided to end production of the 767 freighter program in 2027
findings.use_in_model: Boeing has exited segments when the economics failed and Washington did not react. These were adjacent segments, not the core 737, so they bound rather than settle the question.

findings.topic: US support: the 1997 McDonnell Douglas merger
findings.claim: The FTC cleared Boeing's merger with McDonnell Douglas without conditions on 1 Jul 1997, while saying it was 'troubled' by Boeing's 20-year exclusive airline contracts. The European Commission cleared it on 23 Jul 1997 on condition that Boeing sign no new exclusive deals until 2007. Since then Boeing has been the only US maker of large commercial jets.
findings.source: CNN Money 1997-07-01 https://money.cnn.com/1997/07/01/companies/boeing_a/ ; Boeing release 1997-07-23 https://boeing.mediaroom.com/1997-07-23-Boeing-McDonnell-Douglas-Merger-Gains-a-Positive-Opinion-from-the-European-Commission
findings.quote: Had we proceeded without the approval of the European Commission, we would have potentially faced large fines (Condit)
findings.unit: remaining US large commercial jet maker
findings.use_in_model: US policy created a single national champion. Under Do Nothing, the US would have no domestic narrowbody design authority after 2060. This underpins the H8 doctrine premium, but it is a non-cash argument.

findings.topic: US support: WTO dispute and tariffs
findings.claim: The WTO authorised the US to impose about $7.5B a year of tariffs on EU goods (October 2019), and the US put 15% tariffs on imported Airbus aircraft. The EU was authorised about $3.99B a year over Washington state's Boeing tax incentive and put 15% tariffs on Boeing aircraft. A five-year truce in June 2021 suspended tariffs on $11.5B of trade. EU member states voted in June 2026 to extend their suspension, and the Commission adopted it from 11 July 2026, reportedly open-ended. The subsidy dispute itself is unresolved.
findings.source: 10-K FY2020 p.1369 (B-2509, B-1761); FQ2 2021 call p.683 (B-1825); Bloomberg Tax 2021 https://news.bloombergtax.com/international-trade/eu-u-s-reach-deal-in-bid-to-end-boeing-airbus-trade-spat-3 ; Bloomberg 2026-06-25 https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-25/eu-extends-tariff-suspension-in-boeing-airbus-trade-dispute ; MLex https://www.mlex.com/mlex/trade/articles/2497839
findings.quote: the WTO authorized the U.S. to impose approximately $7.50 billion in annual tariffs on EU products in connection with the EU's provision of eight instances of launch aid subsidies to Airbus
findings.use_in_model: Washington spent 17 years of trade capital defending Boeing against subsidised Airbus, and the 2021 deal says future support must be on market terms. If DC funded an fps launch, Brussels could cite it as launch aid; if Boeing exits, Airbus wins without a fight.

findings.topic: US support: the Export-Import Bank ('Boeing's bank')
findings.claim: Buyers of Boeing products received about 70% of Ex-Im loan guarantees and 35% of all aid in FY2007-14 (Mercatus, an advocacy source). In 2015 Boeing said about 15% of customers used Ex-Im as backstop financing. During the 2015 charter lapse it cut up to several hundred satellite jobs in El Segundo, partly blaming lost Ex-Im financing. The current charter expires on 31 Dec 2026. S.3772 (February 2026) would extend it to 2036; a House draft would extend it to 2031. Boeing signed a July 2026 coalition letter backing a long reauthorisation.
findings.source: FQ2 2015 call p.1757 (BX-0985); FQ2 2014 call p.1941 (B-2447); Mercatus https://www.mercatus.org/publications/federal-fiscal-policy/ex-im-still-boeings-bank ; Fox13/LA Times Aug 2015 https://www.fox13seattle.com/news/boeing-to-lay-off-up-to-several-hundred-employees-in-satellite-division ; Congress.gov S.3772 https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/3772/text ; legis1 https://legis1.com/news/export-import-bank-reauthorization-1-faces-1
findings.quote: We have about 15% of our customers that use Ex-Im financing as backstop financing (Muilenburg)
findings.use_in_model: Export finance is real support for sales, and Boeing uses job cuts as a political lever in DC. A narrowbody exit would weaken Ex-Im's main justification. Small effect on fps cash: a few points of order capture in weaker-credit markets.

findings.topic: US support: CARES Act 2020, offered but declined
findings.claim: The CARES Act set aside $17B in loans for businesses 'critical to maintaining national security', widely seen as aimed at Boeing; Treasury terms allowed the government to take warrants or equity. Calhoun opposed giving the government an equity stake. Boeing raised $25B in bonds on about 30 Apr 2020 and did not apply before the 1 May deadline. Boeing nonetheless publicly thanked Congress for the CARES Act.
findings.source: Gulf News 2020-04-30 https://gulfnews.com/business/aviation/boeing-raising-25b-in-bonds-not-seeking-us-government-funds-1.1588300285488 ; CNBC 2020-04-07 https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/07/coronavirus-house-democrats-urge-boeing-to-take-federal-aid-as-plants-shut-down.html ; Transcripts p.856 (FQ1 2020 call; B-1668) and p.836
findings.quote: we applaud the administration and Congress for working together to pass the CARES Act, which will be critical to supporting the nation's entire aerospace manufacturing sector, which comprise 2.5 million jobs and 17,000 suppliers
findings.use_in_model: Washington's willingness to rescue Boeing acts like an implicit safety net that could soften the fps -$1B downside test. Boeing has shown it will pay market rates to avoid government equity. Model DC launch support as available only with strings that the Board discounts.

findings.topic: US support: the NASA X-66A demonstrator, paused in 2025
findings.claim: NASA committed $425M and Boeing and partners about $725M (about $1.15B in total) to the X-66A truss-braced-wing demonstrator. In January 2025 Ortberg said its results would factor into the next airplane. On 24 Apr 2025 Boeing and NASA paused the flight demonstrator indefinitely and moved engineers to the 777X and MAX, keeping ground research on thin wings. I found no sign it has resumed.
findings.source: FQ4 2024 call p.129 (B-2224); Bernstein Jun 2023 p.322 (B-2062); AIAA 2025-04-25 https://aiaa.org/2025/04/25/nasa-and-boeing-pause-x-66-development-to-focus-on-ultra-thin-wing-design/ ; The Air Current https://theaircurrent.com/feed/dispatches/boeing-shelves-plans-nasa-x-66-flight-demonstrator-ttbw/
findings.quote: we'll look at what comes out of that and how that factors into our next airplane ... we've also got some funding there to support us (Ortberg, Jan 2025)
findings.use_in_model: Government technology money is under $1B, and Boeing put current-programme needs ahead of it. Count federal co-funding as a small fps cost offset, not a driver.

findings.topic: US support: presidential trade deals as a Boeing sales channel
findings.claim: 2025-26 trade diplomacy brought large Boeing commitments: Qatar 130 787s and 30 777Xs (about $96B; up to 210 aircraft), Korean Air 103 aircraft (about $36B; firmed 16 Sep 2026), Japan 100, Indonesia 50, the UK $10B (IAG 32 jets, $13B), and Turkish up to 75 787s ($30B) plus 100 737 MAX. Commerce reported $244B of contracts it helped win in 2025, $215B of them Boeing and GE. Boeing's 2025 net orders were 1,173 against Airbus's 889, its first win since 2018. Analysts (Axios) note some orders would have come anyway.
findings.source: Euronews 2025-05-15 https://www.euronews.com/business/2025/05/15/boeing-secures-landmark-deal-with-qatar-airways-as-trump-deepens-gulf-ties ; Boeing release 2026-09-16 https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-09-16-Boeing,-Korean-Air-Announce-Record-103-Airplane-Order ; Aerospace Global News (Japan) https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/trump-trade-deal-boeing-japan/ ; GMFUS (UK) https://gmfus.org/news/us-uk-economic-prosperity-deal ; Reuters via MarketScreener 2026-01-23 https://uk.marketscreener.com/news/us-commerce-assisted-foreign-contracts-jump-to-244-billion-in-2025-on-boeing-order-gains-ce7e5bdad88af126 ; Axios 2025-07-23 https://www.axios.com/2025/07/23/japan-trade-deal-boeing-trump-tariffs ; The National 2026-01-13
findings.quote: as the largest American exporter ... Boeing is naturally poised to reap significant international business, some of which might've come without trade deals (Axios)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing aircraft are a main currency of US trade diplomacy, so an exit removes a tool DC values. The same deals fill the MAX and widebody backlog, which makes delaying the fps easier. Possible use: a small uplift in fps order capture or price when DC is helping; no change to Do Nothing before 2045.

findings.topic: US support: China reopened to Boeing narrowbodies (May 2026)
findings.claim: After the May 2026 Trump-Xi summit, China committed to 200 Boeing aircraft; Trump cited an option for up to 750 more, which Boeing has not confirmed. Ortberg, who travelled with the President, said his main goal was to reopen China to Boeing narrowbodies after nearly a decade without an order. Chinese airlines are converting the commitment into firm orders one by one.
findings.source: Transcript Digest (4).pdf, PDF p.54 (Bernstein conference, 27 May 2026) and p.27 (conference, 16 Sep 2026); OPB/AP 2026-05-16 https://www.opb.org/article/2026/05/16/trump-and-boeing-say-china-agreed-to-buy-200-aircraft-reopening-a-key-market-for-the-us-planemaker/ ; CNBC 2026-05-14 https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/14/china-boeing-order-airplanes-737-max-trump-says.html
findings.quote: My primary objective was to reopen that market to our narrowbody airplanes. As you know, we haven't had an order in nearly a decade. (Ortberg)
findings.use_in_model: Washington now puts its own capital into keeping Boeing's narrowbody in China. That raises 737 MAX volumes in Do Nothing's early years, and suggests DC would treat a narrowbody exit as a loss in its China bargaining.

findings.topic: US government treatment: DOJ non-prosecution agreement (2025)
findings.claim: Judge O'Connor rejected the July 2024 guilty-plea deal ($243.6M fine) in December 2024. In May 2025 DOJ agreed a non-prosecution deal worth about $1.1B: $444.5M to a victims' fund, a $243.6M fine and about $455M for safety and compliance. On 6 Nov 2025 the judge dismissed the criminal case at DOJ's request, while writing that the deal 'fails to secure the necessary accountability'.
findings.source: CNBC 2025-11-06 https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/06/boeing-criminal-case-737-max-crashes-doj.html ; NPR 2025-05-23 https://www.npr.org/2025/05/23/nx-s1-5409364/boeing-justic-department-737-max-plane-crashes-charges-deal
findings.quote: fails to secure the necessary accountability to ensure the safety of the flying public (Judge O'Connor)
findings.use_in_model: Washington avoided a criminal conviction of its national champion. Boeing benefits from being too important to convict, which is part of the relationship a narrowbody exit would test. This is a non-cash factor and fits the H8 premium.

findings.topic: US leverage: FAA rate cap and the Transportation Secretary's stance
findings.claim: The FAA capped 737 output at 38 a month in January 2024, raised it to 42 on 17 Oct 2025, and cleared 47 after a capstone review announced 27 May 2026. At his January 2025 confirmation hearing Duffy called Boeing 'the largest exporter of American product' needing 'tough love'. In March 2025 he said: 'we're going to put the screws to you'.
findings.source: CNBC 2025-10-17 https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/17/boeing-737-max-production.html ; Lynnwood Times 2026-05-31 https://lynnwoodtimes.com/2026/05/31/737-max/ ; Bloomberg Government Jan 2025 https://news.bgov.com/bloomberg-government-news/trumps-transport-pick-vows-to-cut-red-tape-prioritize-safety ; Jakarta Post/Reuters 2025-03-16 https://www.thejakartapost.com/business/2025/03/16/boeing-lost-trust-of-americans-needs-strict-oversight-us-official-says.html ; FQ4 2024 call p.116 (B-2234)
findings.quote: Boeing is the largest exporter of American product ... they need 'tough love' (Duffy)
findings.use_in_model: Washington directly controls narrowbody cash flow through rate approvals and will use that power. There is no evidence it is tied to product strategy. It mainly adds certification and ramp risk to fps timelines.

findings.topic: Counter-case: congressional pressure changed a product decision (MAX 7, 2024)
findings.claim: In January 2024 Boeing withdrew its request for a time-limited exemption to certify the MAX 7 before an engineered anti-ice fix, after a senator (Calhoun says 'she') objected. Calhoun called the climbdown 'a sound, principled position'.
findings.quote: you want to introduce this new airplane, a derivative, yes, but a new airplane. And 9 months from now, you'll have an engineered solution to it ... it was a sound, principled position to take. (Calhoun)
findings.use_in_model: Pressure from DC has changed Boeing decisions on safety and certification. That is evidence of DC's power, but not of power over whether Boeing launches a programme.

findings.topic: Statements: 'top US exporter' and industrial-base framing
findings.claim: Boeing consistently presents itself to Washington as the top US exporter and part of the industrial base. Examples: 'We're the U.S.'s biggest exporter' (January 2017); aerospace earns about an $80B-plus annual trade surplus (October 2019); the administration understands 'the role that Boeing plays as a top U.S. exporter' and wants to keep 'our U.S. industrial base globally competitive' (April 2025). Former Commerce official Bruce Mehlman (undated quote, in coverage of the 2025 UK deal): Boeing 'is a national champion ... supported by every administration'.
findings.source: Transcripts 2006-2025 PDF p.1521 (25 Jan 2017), p.944 (FQ3 2019, 23 Oct 2019), p.73 and p.75 (FQ1 2025, 23 Apr 2025), p.38 (FQ2 2025, 29 Jul 2025); Mehlman quote via search excerpt (date and outlet not shown)
findings.quote: the administration understands the aerospace industry's importance to our economy broadly and U.S. manufacturing jobs specifically, and is focused on keeping our U.S. industrial base globally competitive for the long term
findings.unit: USD billion annual aerospace trade surplus (Boeing claim)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing has built its political capital on being the champion of US exports and the industrial base. Exiting the largest export segment would undercut that story. This is reputational, non-cash value for H8.

findings.topic: Statements: no official demand for a 737 successor; think-tank case on COMAC
findings.claim: My searches found no US official or congressional statement (2024-2026) demanding a 737 successor or warning against ceding narrowbodies to Airbus or COMAC; this is a gap in what the searches returned. The national-security case comes from think tanks. ITIF (June 2026) says COMAC received at least $72B in subsidies and that lost US airframe know-how could not be rebuilt without massive subsidies. AEI counters that COMAC still lacks FAA and EASA certification. In 2023 Senators Rubio and Rick Scott pressed Commerce to list COMAC as a military end user.
findings.source: ITIF 2026-06-15 https://itif.org/publications/2026/06/15/comac-chinas-looming-threat-to-global-aviation-industry/ ; AEI https://www.aei.org/technology-and-innovation/can-comacs-home-field-advantage-challenge-boeings-737/ ; Sen. Rick Scott 2023-04 https://www.rickscott.senate.gov/2023/4/sens-rick-scott-and-marco-rubio-question-commerce-s-failure-to-include-chinese-state-owned-aerospace-manufacturer-on-meu-list
findings.quote: COMAC ... has received at least $72 billion in subsidies (ITIF, as summarised in search excerpt)
findings.use_in_model: The China argument is real in policy circles but has not yet become pressure on Boeing's product choice. Treat it as a scenario trigger (for example DC offers launch support if COMAC gains Western certification) rather than a current cash value.

findings.topic: US policy toward China aerospace is transactional
findings.claim: In late May 2025 Commerce suspended export licences to COMAC for the C919, including CFM LEAP-1C engines and GE CF34 engines, amid a rare-earths dispute. The suspension was lifted in early July 2025 after a US-China minerals deal in London. China has also halted Boeing deliveries over tariffs (2025) and regulatory issues (2024).
findings.source: ch-aviation https://www.ch-aviation.com/news/172507 ; Caixin 2025-06-03 https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-06-03/us-export-curbs-threaten-chinas-homegrown-jet-ambitions-102326720.html ; Free Malaysia Today/Reuters 2025-05-29 ; FQ1 2025 call p.73 (B-2293); B-2183 p.184
findings.unit: weeks the COMAC licence suspension lasted
findings.use_in_model: Washington treats airliners as a bargaining chip with China and trades it for other aims. Do not assume a durable US policy to keep COMAC out of narrowbodies; that weakens the 'leaving the market to US rivals' argument as a reliable source of DC support.

findings.topic: Industrial-policy precedent: government equity stakes (2025-26)
findings.claim: Washington took equity in strategic firms: Intel 9.9% for $8.9B (22 Aug 2025); MP Materials 15% for $400M from DoD (July 2025); Lithium Americas 5% (1 Oct 2025); Trilogy Metals 10%; Vulcan Elements $50M (November 2025); and a golden share in US Steel with veto rights (June 2025). In April 2026 it negotiated a rescue of up to $500M for Spirit Airlines with warrants or equity; I did not confirm the outcome. One tracker says all completed stakes so far went to semiconductors and critical minerals.
findings.source: CNN via KVIA 2025-11-17 https://kvia.com/news/business-technology/cnn-business-consumer/2025/11/17/uncle-sam-is-outperforming-the-sp-500/ ; Fortune 2026-04-22 https://fortune.com/2026/04/22/trump-administration-500-million-deal-spirit-airlines/ ; farexio https://farexio.com/en/events/us-government-stake-spirit-airlines-2026
findings.use_in_model: There is now a precedent for DC capital in strategic firms, including airline rescue talks. Add a scenario in which DC co-funds the fps for equity or a golden share. This lowers fps cash cost and downside, but Boeing (2020) has valued independence above it; apply a governance cost.

findings.topic: Industrial policy: Lutnick named Boeing in stake discussions
findings.claim: On 26 Aug 2025 Commerce Secretary Lutnick told CNBC the administration was discussing stakes in defense firms and named Lockheed Martin, Boeing and Palantir. He called Lockheed, which gets 97% of revenue from the US government, 'basically an arm of the US government'. Boeing declined to comment. No Boeing stake has been reported since.
findings.source: Al Jazeera 2025-08-26 https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2025/8/26/trump-administration-considers-stake-in-defence-firms-like-lockheed-martin ; Inside Defense https://insidedefense.com/daily-news/lutnicks-talk-government-stake-defense-industry-draws-questions-and-skepticism
findings.quote: basically an arm of the US government (Lutnick, of Lockheed)
findings.unit: % of Lockheed revenue from US government (Lutnick)
findings.use_in_model: Washington has openly considered owning part of Boeing. A permanent narrowbody exit would make Boeing look more like Lockheed (mostly a government supplier), which could invite more state ownership or control. Treat it as a governance risk on both branches, not a cash item.

findings.topic: DC leverage: Boeing's revenue share from US government contracts
findings.claim: The share of Boeing revenue earned under US government contracts (including Foreign Military Sales) was 46% in 2008, 33% in 2012, 23% in 2016, 39% in 2019, 51% in 2020, 40% in 2022, 37% in 2023, 42% in 2024 and 35% in 2025.
findings.source: Boeing 10-Ks in 'Boeing 10ks.pdf' (repo): 2008 p.827, 2012 p.11, 2016 p.978, 2019 p.476, 2020 p.1350, 2022 p.1518, 2023 p.304, 2024 p.2177. FY2025 10-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12927/000162828026004357/ba-20251231.htm (fetch blocked; search excerpt)
findings.quote: In 2024, 42% of our revenues were earned pursuant to U.S. government contracts, which include Foreign Military Sales (FMS) through the U.S. government.
findings.use_in_model: Washington is Boeing's largest single customer, so its goodwill matters. My inference: with no commercial narrowbody after 2060 the US government share would likely exceed 50%, leaving Boeing structurally a defense contractor. That is non-cash value the Board may weigh in H8.

findings.topic: DC leverage: both sixth-generation fighters awarded to Boeing (2025-26)
findings.claim: Trump announced the F-47 award to Boeing on 21 Mar 2025. The value is classified; analysts cite about $20B for development, and Ortberg says it is cost-plus. On 29 Sep 2026 the Navy picked Boeing for F/A-XX (more than $20B). Boeing now holds two of the three US sixth-generation aircraft programmes. Ortberg expects defense revenue growth to rise to 'middle single digit or higher'.
findings.source: DefenseScoop 2025-03-21 https://defensescoop.com/2025/03/21/boeing-ngad-award-air-force-f-47-trump/ ; Defense News 2026-09-29 https://www.defensenews.com/industry/techwatch/2026/09/29/us-navy-selects-boeing-to-build-next-generation-fa-xx-fighter/ ; Transcript Digest (4).pdf p.5 and p.15-16 (FQ3 2026 call, 27 Oct 2026); B-2299 p.62
findings.quote: we achieved a transformational win that will shape the company for decades to come when the U.S. Navy selected Boeing as the winner of the F/A-XX competition (Ortberg)
findings.use_in_model: This cuts both ways. It is goodwill from DC that a hasty commercial exit could strain, but nothing links the awards to commercial choices. It also gives Boeing a credible defense growth path that makes Do Nothing easier to defend to investors. Cost-plus contracts lower group risk and could help fund the fps.

findings.topic: Past behaviour: Boeing paid billions to win and keep DC franchises
findings.claim: Boeing bid aggressively on fixed-price defense development (KC-46, T-7A, MQ-25, VC-25B, Commercial Crew) and took $691M of charges tied to winning T-7A and MQ-25 (2019). It lost $1.6B on these programmes in 2023, plus about $2.0B on KC-46 in 2024; press reported more than $7B of cumulative KC-46 losses by 2023. Calhoun said of Air Force One: 'risks that Boeing probably shouldn't have taken'. In 2025 Ortberg swore off fixed-price development.
findings.source: 10-K FY2019 p.489 (B-1632); 10-K FY2023 p.305 (B-2109); FQ1 2022 call p.613 (BX-0314); FQ4 2024 call p.127 (B-2227); KC-46 totals from Breaking Defense / Defense One Jan 2025 search excerpts https://breakingdefense.com/2025/01/boeing-to-log-1-7b-in-defense-program-losses-in-fourth-quarter/
findings.quote: We've been burned on that on the tanker program ... So we've taken our medicine. We're not going to do that anymore. (Ortberg)
findings.use_in_model: Under earlier leaders Boeing accepted losses for strategic position, which is a precedent for a doctrine premium. The current team has explicitly rejected that approach. Read it as evidence that today's Board will hold the fps to the business-case and downside tests.

findings.topic: DC interest: military aircraft built on commercial production lines
findings.claim: The E-7 Wedgetail (737-based) shows Congress protecting Boeing commercial-derivative programmes. The Pentagon tried to cancel it in FY2026; Congress restored it and required $1.1B to finish two prototypes; in June 2026 the White House budget office (OMB) sought $1.55B more. The 767 freighter ends in 2027, leaving the KC-46 tanker on the 767 line; the P-8 is also 737-based.
findings.source: Air & Space Forces https://www.airandspaceforces.com/pentagon-relents-seeks-funds-for-e-7-wedgetail/ ; Defense News 2026-06-25 https://www.defensenews.com/news/pentagon-congress/2026/06/25/house-backs-155-billion-to-revive-e-7-wedgetail-spares-navy-hawkeye/ ; 10-K FY2024 p.2201
findings.use_in_model: My inference: DoD has a real stake in a living Boeing narrowbody line for future surveillance, tanker and maritime derivatives. That is a concrete lobby for an fps by the 2040s, and it could bring DoD co-funding or military-derivative orders that raise fps value.

findings.topic: DC friction: Air Force One
findings.claim: In May 2025 Trump said 'I'm not happy with Boeing' over the late VC-25B (contracted for delivery in 2024). He accepted a Qatari 747-8 to be converted by L3Harris as an interim Air Force One, bypassing Boeing. Boeing had already taken large VC-25B charges, including $766M in Q3 2022.
findings.source: FlyingMag https://www.flyingmag.com/boeing-could-speed-air-force-one-delivery-as-trump-weighs-qatari-gift/ ; KSL/Reuters https://www.ksl.com/article/51304869/l3harris-working-on-interim-air-force-one-sought-by-trump- ; FQ3 2022 call p.462 (B-1930); BX-0314
findings.quote: I'm not happy with Boeing (Trump)
findings.use_in_model: Washington's favour depends on execution: the President publicly shamed Boeing and switched supplier on a symbolic programme. Brand and DC value come from delivering, which supports the Board's caution on fps execution risk.

findings.topic: Behaviour: lobbying and CEO time spent in Washington
findings.claim: Boeing spent at least $11.9M a year on federal lobbying every year from 2008 to 2024, including $14.4M in 2023, and $2.6M with 60 lobbyists in Q1 2025. Ortberg said in April 2025 that Boeing deals with the administration, up to the President, almost daily. McNerney said in 2012 that working with government was in the country's and Boeing's interest.
findings.source: OpenSecrets via politicalemails.org https://politicalemails.org/messages/1857986 ; Bloomberg Government https://news.bgov.com/bloomberg-government-news/boeings-14-4-million-leads-in-lobbying-spent-among-contractors ; FQ1 2025 call p.76 (B-2290); Shareholder call 2012-05-15 p.2347 (BX-0757)
findings.quote: I don't think a day goes by where we aren't engaged with someone in the administration, including cabinet secretaries and up to POTUS himself. (Ortberg)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing invests heavily in DC influence, which is about 0.02% of revenue. It treats DC as a channel to manage, not a constraint to obey. Expect Boeing to bargain over any fps decision (incentives, Ex-Im, trade deals) rather than defer to it.

findings.topic: Management's stated intent on a new airplane (2026)
findings.claim: In March 2026 CFO Malave said a new programme will come 'at the right time' but 'not any time near'. Market, technology and Boeing must all be ready, and 'none of those 3' are. Ortberg (July and October 2026): 'no change' in new-airplane strategy; a team is defining the aircraft and market timing; investment through 2029 is mainly R&D and technology; resources will shift to new programmes after the 737-7/-10 and 777X. Nobody in management talks about leaving the narrowbody market.
findings.source: Transcript Digest (4).pdf, PDF p.100 (conference, 17 Mar 2026), p.46 (FQ2 2026 call, 28 Jul 2026), p.16 (FQ3 2026 call, 27 Oct 2026)
findings.quote: there will be a day where we have to enter into a new program. That day is not today, and it's not any time near ... it's unrealistic to say that we'll never develop a new program, we will, at the right time. (Malave)
findings.use_in_model: Management describes an eventual launch, not an exit; nobody describes Do Nothing as a strategy. Model the decision as launch timing (later fps) rather than fps versus permanent exit. A late-2030s launch may capture most of the DC and brand value at lower cost.

findings.topic: Counterpoint: Airbus already builds narrowbodies in the US
findings.claim: Airbus opened a second A320-family final-assembly line in Mobile, Alabama on 13 Oct 2025, doubling A320 capacity there. The site has three lines (two A320, one A220) and more than 2,000 employees; it had delivered 100 A220s by July 2025.
findings.source: Airbus press release 2025-10 https://www.airbus.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-10-airbus-inaugurates-second-a320-final-assembly-line-in-the-us ; Fox10 2025-10-13 https://www.fox10tv.com/2025/10/13/airbus-inaugurates-second-a320-final-assembly-line-mobile/
findings.use_in_model: This weakens the claim that ceding narrowbodies sends all the jobs abroad: some final assembly would move to Alabama, though Boeing's 30,000-plus IAM workers and US suppliers would mostly lose. Lower the jobs-based DC penalty on Do Nothing somewhat.

research.summary:
THEME: brand, engineering identity, reputation. Sources: the repo evidence (B-/BX- ids with transcript page), the 2026 Transcript Digest (4) (extracted to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aero-engine-gameboard/95fa875c-ca9d-5564-a6e5-4c9b461d7e56/scratchpad/geo/brand/txt/digest4.txt) and web searches. WebFetch was blocked for axios.com, theharrispoll.com, qz.com, leehamnews.com and richardaboulafia.com, so web items rest on search excerpts. The 2026 Axios Harris rank for Boeing was not found.

1. Since 1997, finance has won almost every product decision. Boeing ended the 757 (2004) and cancelled the Sonic Cruiser (2002). It chose the MAX over the clean sheet its own engineers wanted (2011), and shelved the NMA (2020). It spent $43.1B on buybacks from Q1 2013 to Q1 2019, about 2.2x its total R&D for 2013-18 ($19.3B, my calculation). Muilenburg stated the rule outright: "It will not be based on market share." The one exception points toward the fps. When narrowbody share was threatened (American Airlines in July 2011), Boeing changed course within weeks to protect "years of near-term market share". It still took the cheapest option, but the MAX phase-out world has no cheap option left.

2. Measured reputation costs came from failures in execution, not from declining to launch. The MAX cost about $20B directly: $8.3B to customers, $6.3B in added programme cost and about $5B of abnormal production costs. Market value fell from about $240B to about $112B. Moody's cut Boeing to Baa3, and Boeing needed a $24B equity raise. Buyers came back fast once supply did. Boeing's net orders were -87 in 2019 and 377 in 2024, then 1,173 in 2025 against Airbus's 889. Brand Finance shows the brand rising 34% to $24.4B in 2026, with no new airplane. Passengers say they will avoid the MAX, but only 3% rank aircraft type first. So the record does not support a large cash "brand premium" for launching. The bigger brand risk is launching and failing: the 787 ran about 5x its first budget.

3. Talent is two-sided. Boeing can hire without a programme: 10,000 engineers in 2022, a 4% applicant acceptance rate in 2026, and a 4-year SPEEA deal in October 2026. The F-47 and F/A-XX wins also give engineers frontier work, which the 1990s-2011 "only design team in America" argument lacked. Experience is what erodes. Engineer tenure fell from 16.4 to 12.6 years. Benkard measured experience depreciating about 4% a month on the L-1011. RAND found design starts per team falling from 2.5 per decade to about 1 per two decades.

4. History offers both endings for an exit. Lockheed left airliners in 1981 after about $2.5B of L-1011 losses and became the largest defense prime, with a much lower equity beta. McDonnell Douglas underinvested, fell to about 5% share and was absorbed in 1997, a "slow death" over about 30 years. Do Nothing with run-off to 2060 resembles the MD path more than Lockheed's clean exit (my inference).

5. Behaviour on jobs. Boeing does cut deeply when it must: 62% of its workforce in 1969-71, 10% in 2020 and 10% in 2024. It also pays to keep capability: about $5B to hold the 737 system through the grounding, $4.2B of 747-8 charges absorbed, and about $46B of commercial operating losses over 2019-25 without exiting.

How this could move the decision (my inference). Brand and engineering identity are real in what leaders say. Ortberg: "Boeing's an airplane company... we need to develop a new airplane." Boeing has also done preparatory work (a team defining a 757-size single-aisle, and engineers to move to new programmes after 777X). But behaviour bounds the value. Enter it as a soft doctrine premium inside the H8 $2B cap, about $0.5-2B, not as cash. It cannot close the $4B gap at 10.5%. At 8.1%, where the fps beats Do Nothing but not a 787 Re-engine alone, it can decide only if that gap is under the cap. Counter-terms to show: a lower cost of equity for a defense-heavier Boeing, and the overrun tail risk of a rushed launch.

findings.topic: Bet-the-company history: 707
findings.claim: Bill Allen put company money into the Dash 80 jet prototype before any customer had committed. The KC-135 and 707 orders followed, with Pan Am ordering 20 707s in October 1955.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_367-80 ; https://www.airspacemag.com/history-of-flight/seven-oh-seven-180971257 (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: A historical precedent for a doctrine premium. It is not a cash term: the bet was small next to a $60-65B fps.
findings.quote: Allen had the company put $16 million into the Dash 80 before any customer had committed

findings.topic: Bet-the-company history: 747 and the Boeing Bust
findings.claim: Allen reportedly said the 747 could ruin Boeing. In the 1969-71 bust that followed, Boeing employment fell from a peak of 100,800 (1967) to 38,690 (April 1971), a 62% cut (my calculation). This was the era of the 'last person leaving Seattle' billboard.
findings.source: https://www.historylink.org/file/20923 ; https://jpbtransconsulting.com/tag/jumbo-jet/ (search excerpts)
findings.direction: mixed: Boeing did bet the company, and also cut 62% of jobs when it had to
findings.use_in_model: Counter-evidence to the idea that jobs pressure binds Boeing: it has made deep cuts before. Supports keeping any jobs premium inside H8, not as a hard constraint.
findings.quote: Will the last person leaving SEATTLE -- Turn out the lights

findings.topic: Design-team retention precedent: C-5A to 747
findings.claim: After Boeing lost the C-5A competition to Lockheed in 1965, the team led by Joe Sutter moved to the 747. Boeing used a commercial programme to keep a design team at work.
findings.source: https://magazine.washington.edu/feature/from-humble-beginnings-joseph-sutter-became-the-father-of-the-747 ; https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/systems/aircraft/b747-history.htm (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: A qualitative precedent for the talent-retention argument. In 2026 the defense side has new frontier work (F-47, F/A-XX), so the argument is weaker today.
findings.quote: Sutter knew he would head up the new project as soon as the Air Force gave the C-5A to Lockheed

findings.topic: 787: technology bet and overrun
findings.claim: The 787 replaced the cancelled Sonic Cruiser. Its first budget was about $6B over about 4 years; reported programme cost topped $32B, and deferred production cost was about $27.7B in 2015. Boeing R&D averaged $3.6B a year (5.69% of revenue) over 2004-2012 and peaked at $6.5B (9.5%) in 2009.
findings.source: Repo profiles/boeing/financials.md section 3 (CapIQ); https://www.thestand.org/2016/04/mcnerneys-legacy-29-billion-in-787-bills/ ; https://leehamnews.com/2015/10/19/do-the-boeing-787-sums-add-up/ (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (tail risk) / toward fps (the 787 became a franchise)
findings.use_in_model: Calibrate fps overrun tail risk in the -$1B downside test. A prestige launch that overruns damages the brand as well as the NPV.
findings.quote: 787-era intensity (5.69%) is the practical ceiling for R&D
findings.unit: $B reported programme cost vs ~$6B first budget

findings.topic: Prestige dropped for economics: Sonic Cruiser
findings.claim: Boeing cancelled the Mach 0.98 Sonic Cruiser on 20 December 2002 after airlines put operating cost ahead of speed, and announced the efficient 7E7 on 29 January 2003. Boeing drops prestige concepts that customers will not pay for.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_Sonic_Cruiser ; https://aerospaceweb.org/aircraft/jetliner/sonic_cruiser/ (search excerpts)
findings.direction: neutral (swapped one new airplane for another)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing's 'technology brand' means customer economics. A brand premium should attach to an fps that clears customer value, not to novelty.
findings.quote: airlines generally preferred lower operating costs over higher speed

findings.topic: 2011 MAX decision: share defence over clean sheet
findings.claim: In July 2011 American Airlines split a 460-jet order (260 Airbus, 200 Boeing), and Boeing re-engined the 737 within weeks. McNerney said a clean sheet would have put 'years of near-term market share strength at risk'. Albaugh said many engineers, himself included, wanted a new plane offering a 20% efficiency gain, but non-recurring cost unknowns ruled it out.
findings.source: Repo B-1038 (Analyst Day 2015-05-12, p1765); B-0532 (Credit Suisse 2011-11-30, p2455); https://www.heraldnet.com/2011/07/20/american-orders-460-jets-including-re-engined-boeing-737/
findings.direction: toward fps in a MAX phase-out world (Boeing acts when narrowbody share is threatened) / toward Do Nothing (it picked the cheapest response)
findings.use_in_model: Inference: when no derivative is available, the 2011 share-defence reflex favours the fps. Gives a doctrine premium a basis, within the $2B cap.
findings.quote: we selected the 737 MAX derivative ... rather than pursue a higher risk, higher cost clean sheet design ... that will have placed years of near-term market share strength at risk
findings.unit: % efficiency of the forgone clean sheet

findings.topic: Stated rule: business case, not market share
findings.claim: Muilenburg in 2016: a new or modified narrowbody would be launched on business-case analysis, 'not ... market share'. In 2018: 'We're not going to launch this airplane unless the business case makes good sense'. The NMA was never launched.
findings.use_in_model: Supports the Board's $1B business-case test as the binding rule and argues for keeping soft premiums small.
findings.quote: It will not be based on market share. We are not in business just to chase market share.

findings.topic: NMA shelved; Calhoun
findings.claim: Calhoun shelved the NMA in January 2020. He said Boeing would do a new airplane, but saw no big deficiencies in the narrowbody fleet. In 2022 he said no new airplane 'until we know we're capable', and in 2023 'not before 35'.
findings.use_in_model: Shows the 'we will do one' identity statement coexisting with years of deferral. Discount identity rhetoric when estimating how likely Boeing is to launch.
findings.quote: me not immediately signing up to the NMA is not -- is me not wanting to do new airplanes. We'll do one.

findings.topic: Buybacks vs R&D, 2013-2019
findings.claim: Boeing spent $43.1B on buybacks from Q1 2013 to Q1 2019 (104% of profits), against total R&D of $19.3B over 2013-2018, so buybacks were about 2.2x R&D (my calculation). In December 2018, after the first MAX crash, the board approved a further $20B, later shelved. Long-term pay was tied to shareholder returns.
findings.source: Lazonick & Sakinc via https://fortune.com/longform/boeing-737-max-crisis-shareholder-first-culture and https://nakedcapitalism.com/2020/03/boeing-crashes-43-billion-in-share-buybacks-turn-into-existential-threat.html (search excerpts); repo financials.md section 1; repo B-1048 (2015-05-12, p1772)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (past doctrine) / toward fps (backlash against that era)
findings.use_in_model: Baseline evidence that the Board's doctrine has favoured capital return over development. A brand premium cuts against this record, so keep it within H8 and log it.
findings.quote: we also revised our long-term management compensation structure to more closely align to shareholder returns, which ... reinforces the culture of financial discipline

findings.topic: Culture debate after the McDonnell Douglas merger
findings.claim: Stonecipher (CEO 2003-05) is widely quoted as saying he changed Boeing so it is 'run like a business rather than a great engineering firm' (wording not traced to a dated transcript). HQ moved to Chicago (2001) and Arlington (2022); Aboulafia called the 2022 move a missed opportunity. Ortberg chose to be based in Seattle.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Stonecipher ; https://news.yahoo.com/boeing-set-move-headquarters-arlington-170611185.html ; https://virginiabusiness.com/?p=169725 (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Qualitative backing for an 'engineering identity' doctrine premium under Ortberg, capped by H8.
findings.quote: When people say I changed the culture of Boeing, that was the intent, so that it is run like a business rather than a great engineering firm

findings.topic: Incentives moved away from new designs
findings.claim: McNerney (2015) changed the reward system to value cost and productivity 'as highly as' a new leading-edge wing. Muilenburg (2014) wanted the best engineers on 'innovative reuse' rather than 'the new thing'.
findings.use_in_model: Explains why the NMA debates ended in deferral. Evidence that engineering-identity arguments lost inside Boeing for a decade.
findings.quote: In the past, we may have said our best engineers are working on the new thing, now we want our best engineers working on innovative reuse

findings.topic: Measured MAX crisis cost
findings.claim: Boeing recorded an $8.259B customer-consideration charge in 2019 (net of $500M insurance), $6.3B of higher 737 programme cost, and about $5B of abnormal production costs. Analysts put direct costs at about $20B and indirect costs above $60B.
findings.source: Repo B-1628 (10-K FY2019, p473); B-1650 (p517); B-1675 (FQ1 2020 call, p860); https://en.wikipedia.com/wiki/Financial_impact_of_the_Boeing_737_MAX_groundings (search excerpt)
findings.direction: neutral (brand cost came from an engineering failure)
findings.use_in_model: The largest brand costs arise from failed execution. Use them to size fps downside/tail risk, not a Do Nothing brand penalty.
findings.quote: we recorded an earnings charge of $8,259 million, net of insurance recoveries of $500 million, in 2019 ... potential concessions and other considerations to customers

findings.topic: Paying to keep the workforce
findings.claim: Boeing kept its 737 workforce and infrastructure through the 2020 production suspension, about 12,000 at Renton, with about 3,000 reassigned. It expensed about $5B of abnormal costs. Calhoun said Boeing avoided layoffs 'even through the suspension', then cut about 10% of its roughly 160,000 staff in 2020 because of COVID.
findings.source: Repo B-1618 (FQ4 2019 call, p898); B-1672 and B-1673 (FQ1 2020 call, p858-859); B-1789 (10-K FY2020, p1393); https://www.cnbc.com/2020/01/06/boeing-reassigs-thousands-of-737-max-workers-while-supplier-spirit-mulls-layoffs.html
findings.direction: toward fps (Boeing pays billions to preserve capability)
findings.use_in_model: A revealed-preference anchor for valuing capability: about $5B over about 20 months, which also covered supply-chain costs, not only labour (inference). Supports pricing capability loss under Do Nothing.
findings.quote: This includes costs related to our decision to maintain the 737 production infrastructure, including labor during the suspension and low rate production

findings.topic: Customer order behaviour after crises
findings.claim: In 2019 Boeing finished with net -51 narrowbody orders while Airbus booked over 700. In 2024 Boeing had 569 gross and 377 net orders (317 after ASC 606) against Airbus's 826 net. In 2025 Boeing booked 1,173 net against Airbus's 889, its first win since 2018.
findings.source: https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2025/jan/19/crisis-hit-boeing-delivered-less-than-half-as-many ; https://www.euronews.com/2025/01/15/boeings-aircraft-deliveries-and-orders-in-2024-reflect-the-companys-rough-year ; https://www.bostonwarwick.com/blog/boeing-reclaims-the-order-crown-inside-the-2025-airbusboeing-scorecard/ (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (customer brand damage proved transient)
findings.use_in_model: Airlines buy on delivery slots and price in a duopoly. Do not add a large permanent brand penalty to Do Nothing for the crisis years.
findings.quote: Boeing booked 1,173 net orders versus 889 for Airbus ... the first time Boeing outsold Airbus since 2018

findings.topic: Narrowbody share already lost
findings.claim: In 2024 Airbus delivered 602 A320neo-family jets against 260 737 MAX. At end-July 2026 the backlog was 7,574 A320neo plus 574 A220 against 4,817 737 MAX, so Airbus holds about 63% (my calculation). Analysts cite about 40% as the minimum for a duopoly.
findings.source: https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2026/08/11/airbus-and-boeing-report-july-2026-commercial-aircraft-orders-and-deliveries/ ; https://flightglobal.com/airframers/boeing-aims-to-evenly-split-narrowbody-aircraft-market-share/143509.article (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward fps (a franchise near the duopoly floor)
findings.use_in_model: Set the share and widebody-erosion sliders from a base already near 37-40%. A Do Nothing run-off starts below the duopoly threshold.
findings.quote: Analysts saw about 40% as the minimum Boeing needed to keep a duopoly
findings.unit: % Boeing share of narrowbody backlog, July 2026 (my calc)

findings.topic: Customer defection: United
findings.claim: After the door plug, United took the MAX 10 out of its fleet plan, told Boeing to build MAX 9s instead, and in April 2024 leased 35 A321neos for 2026-27. Its firm MAX 10 order was not cancelled.
findings.source: https://www.flightglobal.com/airlines/united-airlines-removes-max-10-from-fleet-plan-over-expected-delay/156596.article ; https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-03-12/united-ceo-tells-boeing-to-stop-making-its-long-delayed-max-10s (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Defection follows certification and availability failures. Reputational erosion should be modelled through delivery reliability, not brand image.
findings.quote: United has told Boeing to stop building Max 10s for its fleet
findings.unit: A321neo leased to replace MAX 10 slots

findings.topic: Price concessions on the relaunch
findings.claim: Ryanair's December 2020 order for 75 MAX ($9B list) was expected to carry a discount 'well over two-thirds', partly in lieu of grounding compensation. O'Leary called it 'very modest'. Calhoun said Boeing did not need to 'discount our way into the marketplace'.
findings.source: https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/03/ryanair-agrees-to-buy-75-boeing-737-max-jets-in-boost-for-the-planemaker.html ; https://www.lse.co.uk/news/update-3-ryanair-buys-75-boeing-max-jets-in-largest-order-since-grounding-agzvajkey1vp439.html (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Bounds the price cost of a reputation hit, an unconfirmed source expectation. Relevant to the C5 price-fade term if a Do Nothing run-off brings customer leverage.
findings.quote: expected to win an even bigger discount of well over two-thirds in return for the MAX relaunch

findings.topic: Passenger avoidance: said vs did
findings.claim: Surveys found 44% of fliers would wait a year to fly the MAX (Barclays, 2019) and over half 'not likely' to fly it (Reuters/Ipsos, 2020-21). Yet only 3% said aircraft type was the most important factor. Kayak filter use rose 15x after January 2024, with no absolute figures released.
findings.source: https://benzinga.com/analyst-ratings/analyst-color/19/05/13682625/barclays-downgrades-boeing-after-survey-shows-long-road-to-regaining-passenger-conf ; https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=2605059 ; https://www.phocuswire.com/Kayak-sees-15X-increase-in-aircraft-filter-usage-following-Alaska-Airlines-incident (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (passenger sentiment does not move fleet decisions)
findings.use_in_model: Do not add a passenger-demand brand term. Stated avoidance far exceeds revealed behaviour.
findings.quote: Only three percent said the aircraft type was the most important factor
findings.unit: % of fliers ranking aircraft type first

findings.topic: Reputation polls (Axios Harris)
findings.claim: In 2024 Boeing's reputation score fell 10 points to 65.9, the poll's largest drop. In 2025 it was flat at about 65, 13 points below 2019, ranking No. 90 for trust and ethics and No. 93 for vision and growth. Its 2026 rank could not be retrieved (axios.com and theharrispoll.com were blocked).
findings.source: https://www.axios.com/2024/05/24/boeing-airline-reputation-harris-poll ; https://www.axios.com/2025/05/22/reputation-decline-tesla-boeing ; https://247wallst.com/investing/2025/05/22/in-america-only-one-brand-is-worse-than-trump/ (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Inference: the weak 'vision and growth' score is the dimension a launch would address. Opinion only, so it can support a small doctrine premium, not a cash term.
findings.quote: Boeing's reputation score has seen a 13-point decline since 2019, coming in at No. 90 for trust and ethics and No. 93 for vision and growth

findings.topic: Brand value (Brand Finance)
findings.claim: Brand Finance valued the Boeing brand at $22.7B in 2020 (-29%) and $16.2B in 2024 (-8%). It recovered to $18.2B in 2025 and $24.4B in 2026 (+34%). In 2026 Airbus overtook it at $27.2B (+63%), helped by deliveries, backlog and defence.
findings.source: https://brandfinance.com/press-releases/airbus-takes-the-title-of-worlds-most-valuable-aerospace-defence-brand ; https://brandirectory.com/aerospace-and-defence (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (brand recovered on execution, without a new airplane)
findings.use_in_model: Brand value tracks deliveries and the defence cycle. Do not credit the fps with brand value as such. A Do Nothing exit decade (2045-60) is outside this evidence.
findings.quote: Boeing (brand value up 34% to USD24.4 billion) ... has ceded leadership

findings.topic: Market value lost
findings.claim: Boeing's market capitalisation was about $240B in March 2019. In 2024 it was about $112-115B, and Airbus (about $140B) passed Boeing in market value for the first time since Airbus listed in 2000.
findings.source: https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/opinion-five-part-strategy-boeing-ceo-dave-calhoun ; https://sofi.com/article/market-news/what-boeings-trouble-means-for-airbus-market-share (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: About $125B of equity value lost in a crisis of engineering credibility. Context for the Board's sensitivity to reputation and for the $2B rating buffer.
findings.quote: Airbus valued at nearly $140 billion, and Boeing at about $112 billion

findings.topic: Credit rating and equity raise
findings.claim: Moody's cut Boeing to Baa3 in April 2024, one notch above junk. In October 2024 Boeing raised $24.25B of equity and mandatory convertibles, the largest primary US equity offering on record, to protect its rating. Fitch (June 2025) and S&P (31 October 2025) moved to stable at BBB-. Ortberg's stated priority is debt, to be 'solidly investment grade' before the next airplane.
findings.source: https://www.ifre.com/equities/2047759/boeing-boosts-turnaround-hopes-with-us24.25bn-of-equity ; https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/boeing-outlook-revised-to-stable-by-sp-on-increasing-production-93CH-4325197 ; repo BX-1305 (Morgan Stanley 2025-09-11, p30)
findings.use_in_model: Supports the $2B rating-buffer rule. A brand premium cannot override a launch that endangers BBB-.
findings.quote: we want to be solidly investment grade. And we need to be there for the next-generation airplane

findings.topic: Legal and reputational settlements
findings.claim: Under the 2025 non-prosecution agreement Boeing admits conspiring to obstruct an FAA investigation and pays $1.1B. Judge O'Connor dismissed the case on 6 November 2025 while saying the deal lacked accountability. The 2021 deferred prosecution agreement had cost $2.5B.
findings.source: https://www.claimsjournal.com/news/national/2025/11/06/333951.htm ; https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/boeing-paying-1-1b-doj-dismisses-criminal-fraud-case-families-victims-crashes-object-deal (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Tail cost of engineering and safety failures. Belongs in fps execution-risk sizing, not in Do Nothing.
findings.quote: fails to secure the necessary accountability to ensure the safety of the flying public

findings.topic: Talent: 'only design team in America' argument
findings.claim: In 2011-12 Albaugh argued Boeing had the only active US airplane design teams, so young aero engineers 'are going to come and work with us', and that half its engineers could retire within 5 years.
findings.use_in_model: Supports a talent component in the doctrine premium. Weakened in 2026 because the F-47 and F/A-XX now offer frontier design work.
findings.quote: there aren't any active airplane design teams in the United States of America other than the Boeing company

findings.topic: Talent: attrition vs hiring
findings.claim: In 2022 SPEEA lost 1,375 engineers from January to November, 560 of them in November alone (a pension-timing effect), out of about 57,600 Boeing engineers. Boeing hired about 9,000-10,000 engineers that year. Calhoun said they 'joined because of the mission'. The FT (December 2024, citing SPEEA data) reported average engineer tenure falling from 16.4 to 12.6 years over a decade; Boeing says voluntary attrition stays in the low single digits.
findings.source: Repo B-1941 (Investor Day 2022-11-02, p419); B-2035 (BofA 2023-03-22, p369); https://www.adn.com/nation-world/2022/12/07/boeing-lost-hundreds-of-experienced-seattle-area-engineers-last-month/ ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/average-tenure-of-boeing-engineers-drops-over-past-decade-ft-reports (search excerpts)
findings.direction: mixed: hiring is easy (toward Do Nothing), experience erodes (toward fps)
findings.use_in_model: Value lost experience, not headcount. Use it in a capability-decay term for Do Nothing and for a later re-entry option.
findings.quote: What really happened in this process is we were forced to hire 10,000 engineers ... they joined because of the mission

findings.topic: Talent in 2026: employer brand is strong
findings.claim: CFO Malave in March 2026 cited about a 4% applicant acceptance rate and high retention of technical staff, adding 'we pretty much have the employment levels that we need'. He also said 'there will be a day where we have to enter into a new program. That day is not today'. Ortberg reportedly said he was 'not too worried about a brain drain' while engineers wait (Seattle Times; not verified).
findings.source: Transcript Digest (4).pdf, Boeing Company Conference Presentation 17 Mar 2026, p14-15 (scratch extract digest4.txt lines 4708-4800)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (no hiring crisis without a launch)
findings.use_in_model: Do not add a hiring-cost penalty to Do Nothing for 2026-2035. Talent erosion is a post-2035 run-off effect at most.
findings.quote: We've got like a 4% acceptance rate for applicants in the company

findings.topic: Engineers' contract secured
findings.claim: On 1 October 2026 SPEEA ratified a 4-year contract covering about 17,000 engineers and technical staff, with a 10% guaranteed raise; the professional unit voted 67.62% in favour (7,895 to 3,780). It was the first full negotiation in 14 years. Ortberg had warned that a strike would shut down 777X certification.
findings.source: https://lynnwoodtimes.com/2026/10/02/speea-contract/ ; https://qz.com/boeing-speea-engineers-technical-workers-ratify-contract-100226 (search excerpts); Transcript Digest (4).pdf, Conference 16 Sep 2026 p10 and FQ3 2026 call 27 Oct 2026 p4
findings.use_in_model: Engineering labour is stable to about 2030, the fps launch window. No talent-loss shock in the launch-year valuation.
findings.quote: If we did have a strike, essentially the 777 certification program shuts down until we get the engineers back

findings.topic: Cost of losing a design/production team (academic)
findings.claim: Benkard (AER 2000) found 'organizational forgetting' on the Lockheed L-1011 (250 built over 14 years): accumulated experience depreciated about 4% a month, about 39% a year compounded (my calculation). RAND (1992) found design starts per team fell from 2.5 per decade in the 1950s to about 1 every two decades.
findings.source: https://www.nber.org/papers/w7127.pdf ; https://www.minneapolisfed.org/article/2011/is-forgetting-a-problem ; RAND 1992 via https://airandspaceforces.com/PDF/MagazineArchive/Magazine%20Documents/1992/November%201992/1192chart.pdf (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Inference: if Do Nothing leaves no narrowbody design work after the MAX 10, the cost of any later re-entry rises. Use it to justify a capability-decay slider, or to value the option to re-enter.
findings.quote: strong support for organizational forgetting

findings.topic: Boeing's own plan: move engineers to new programmes
findings.claim: On the FQ3 2026 call, Ortberg said a team in product development is defining the new airplane and its market timing. He said that as 737 and 777X development finishes, 'you will see a shift of resources and spending ... to new programs'. Malave added that the cash outlook includes the needed R&D, which is 'not significant types of investments'.
findings.source: Transcript Digest (4).pdf, Boeing FQ3 2026 Earnings Call 27 Oct 2026, p16 (digest4.txt lines 805-826)
findings.direction: toward fps (Boeing intends to keep the design team busy)
findings.use_in_model: Pre-launch engineering is already funded. Do Nothing would need an explicit decision to idle that team, a signal the Board weighs. Fits within the H8 premium.
findings.quote: When we finish the 777 program, you will see a shift of resources and spending from those development programs to new programs.

findings.topic: Ortberg identity statements and timing
findings.claim: Ortberg in 2024: 'Boeing's an airplane company ... we need to develop a new airplane', subject to stabilisation and the balance sheet. In 2025 he set three conditions: market, technology and Boeing ready. In July 2026 he called the next airplane the chance to change Boeing's share of industry profit, and said timing is 'moving to the right' and needs 'a couple more years' of financial repair.
findings.source: Repo B-2217 (FQ3 2024 call, p137); BX-1296 (Bernstein 2025-05-29, p60); Transcript Digest (4).pdf FQ2 2026 call 28 Jul 2026 p14; https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/20/boeing-ceo-ortberg-airbus-farnborough-737max.html ; https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/manufacturing-supply-chain/interview-why-boeings-ceo-sees-next-narrowbody-moving-right (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Leadership doctrine leans to launching eventually. In the game this supports a doctrine premium for the fps against Do Nothing (exit) of up to the $2B H8 cap, not a premium for launching early.
findings.quote: Boeing's an airplane company. And at the right time in the future, we need to develop a new airplane

findings.topic: Pre-launch work reported (2025-26)
findings.claim: The WSJ (30 September 2025) reported early-stage 737-successor work: a senior product leader appointed, flight-deck design under way and talks with Rolls-Royce. Bloomberg (May 2026) reported a single-aisle closer in size to the 757, evolutionary rather than radical, with launch around the turn of the decade. Boeing said it remains focused on recovery.
findings.source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-30/boeing-plans-new-airplane-to-succeed-737-max-wsj-reports ; https://aviationa2z.com/index.php/2026/05/14/boeing-plans-new-single-aisle-jet-larger-than-737-max-10/ (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Evidence that the real Boeing treats a successor as the base case. Consistent with an evolutionary, cheaper fps; check that the fps cost assumption is not a moonshot.
findings.quote: initial design preferences point to a single-aisle airliner that prioritises evolution over revolution

findings.topic: Defense brand independent of commercial reputation
findings.claim: During the commercial crisis Boeing won the USAF F-47 (March 2025) and the Navy F/A-XX (29 September 2026, over $20B of full-scale development). It is now the exclusive US sixth-generation fighter maker; Ortberg called F/A-XX a 'testament to our innovation, our team and trust'.
findings.source: https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-09-29-U-S-Navy-Selects-Boeing-for-F-A-XX-Program ; https://breakingdefense.com/2026/09/boeing-navy-ngad-faxx-next-gen-fighter-competition-northrop/ ; Transcript Digest (4).pdf FQ3 2026 call p5
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (no measurable defense spillover; engineers have frontier work outside commercial)
findings.use_in_model: Do not add a defense-sales penalty to Do Nothing. Discount the talent argument for the fps because defense now absorbs top design talent (inference).
findings.quote: To be selected for another sixth-generation fighter program is a testament to our innovation, our team and trust we've built with our customers

findings.topic: Exit precedent: Lockheed (counter-evidence)
