findings.claim: Lockheed lost about $2.5B on the L-1011, announced the phase-out in December 1981 (last delivery 1984), and never returned to airliners; it became the largest US defense prime. Today Lockheed's equity beta is about 0.1-0.3 against Boeing's 1.2-1.4.
findings.source: https://www.slashgear.com/1959677/why-did-lockheed-martin-stop-making-commercial-planes ; https://www.allinvestview.com/compare/BA-vs-LMT/ (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: An exit need not destroy a US aerospace brand. Inference: a defense-heavier Boeing could carry a lower cost of equity, so show a WACC offset as counter-weight to any franchise or brand penalty.
findings.quote: Lockheed ultimately lost $2.5 billion on the program and exited commercial aviation entirely in 1981

findings.topic: Exit precedent: McDonnell Douglas slow decline
findings.claim: McDonnell Douglas underinvested in airliners and had not designed an all-new one since the late 1960s; the MD-12 never proceeded. Its share fell to about 5-6% of orders by 1996, it would have needed about $15B to compete again, and it merged into Boeing in 1997 for about $14B. Aviation Week called it a 30-year 'slow death'.
findings.source: https://leehamnews.com/2017/09/25/pontifications-revisionist-history/ ; https://australiancompetitionlaw.org/intmergerlaw/cases/boeing.html ; https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/program-management/opinion-will-boeing-become-next-mcdonnell-douglas (search excerpts)
findings.use_in_model: Do Nothing with MAX run-off to 2060 resembles the MD path, not Lockheed's clean exit (inference). Supports the franchise terms (stranded overhead, widebody erosion) already in franchise.py.
findings.quote: the slow death of Douglas Aircraft took 30 years

findings.topic: Boeing stays in commercial through huge losses
findings.claim: Boeing Commercial Airplanes lost about $45.9B of operating profit cumulatively over 2019-2025 (my sum of the repo CapIQ/GS rows) without exiting commercial. Its share of Boeing revenue went from 57% (2018) to 34% (2024) to 46% (2025).
findings.source: Repo profiles/boeing/financials.md section 2 (BCA table) and section 8a
findings.direction: toward fps (revealed commitment) - with the caveat that exit was never a live option given the backlog
findings.use_in_model: Context. A narrowbody exit would make Boeing a defense-majority company, a change of identity the Board has never chosen even at -86% BCA margins. It supports, but does not size, a doctrine premium.

findings.topic: Tolerating losses on an iconic line: 747-8
findings.claim: Boeing kept the 747-8 going through a $685M reach-forward loss (2008) and $1.352B (2009), saying 'We don't intend to kill the program'. Press tallied about $4.2B of charges. The last 747 was delivered on 31 January 2023.
findings.source: Repo B-0143 (FQ4 2008 call, p2849); B-0192 (FQ1 2009 call, p2834); B-0563 (10-K FY2011, p1215); https://fortune.com/2023/01/31/boeing-delivering-last-iconic-747-jumbo-jet-ending-era-plane-revolutionized-travel/
findings.direction: mixed (tolerated losses for years, then ended the icon)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing will absorb a few $B for an iconic franchise but eventually ends it on the numbers. Roughly consistent with the $2B H8 cap.
findings.quote: Is it enough to kill the program? I don't think so. ... We don't intend to kill the program.

findings.topic: Segment exits: 757 (2004) and Embraer JV (2020)
findings.claim: Boeing ended the 757 in October 2004 because the business case for a successor did not close, leaving the segment Airbus filled with the A321neo (about 70% of A320neo backlog in 2026). It walked away from the $4.2B Embraer deal in April 2020 in its cash crisis and settled for $150M in September 2024.
findings.source: https://www.businessinsider.in/boeing-made-a-major-mistake-12-years-ago-that-left-its-customers-in-the-lurch/amp_articleshow/52452768.cms ; https://www.ch-aviation.com/news/144833-boeing-settles-failed-commercial-aviation-jv-with-embraer ; https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2026/04/14/airbus-and-boeing-report-march-2026-commercial-aircraft-orders-and-deliveries/ (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (precedent of exits) / toward fps (the 757 gap became Airbus's A321 dominance)
findings.use_in_model: Counter-evidence that prestige did not stop exits. The 757 case shows the long-run share cost of leaving a segment, which feeds the C4 widebody/share-erosion slider. Brazil, which owns Embraer, is a US Major Non-NATO Ally.
findings.quote: Many in the aviation industry believe that in October 2004 Boeing ended B757 production a decade too soon

findings.topic: Technology identity: R&D and demonstrators
findings.claim: Boeing R&D was $3.6B a year over 2023-2025 (4.62% of revenue), against 5.69% in the 787 era. The ecoDemonstrator has tested more than 260 technologies since 2012, 28% of which reached products. The NASA X-66A flight programme ($425M from NASA, about $725M from Boeing and partners) was paused in 2025, with ground work on the thin wing continuing.
findings.source: Repo financials.md section 3; https://www.boeing.com/innovation/sustainability/ecodemonstrator ; https://simpleflying.com/boeing-nasa-sustainable-flight-demonstrator-aircraft-project/ ; https://avweb.com/aviation-news/boeing-nasa-pause-x-66a-flight-program/ (search excerpts)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing short-term (flagship demonstrator cut when cash was tight)
findings.use_in_model: The science and technology brand is maintained at low cost through ecoDemonstrator. Boeing sacrificed the visible X-66A when cash bound, so brand-led R&D gives way to finance.
findings.quote: Boeing and NASA paused the X-66A due to shifting priorities and limited resources

findings.topic: Analyst opinion: a narrowbody successor is make-or-break for brand and talent
findings.claim: Aboulafia (April 2024) wrote that Boeing's ability to design new aircraft 'has atrophied across the board', and that skipping a clean sheet signals Boeing is no longer an engineering company and makes recruiting harder. Bloomberg's Thomas Black (30 September 2025) called the 737 replacement 'make-or-break' for restoring Boeing's standard of excellence. Fortune (1 June 2026) credits Ortberg with an engineering-first culture but asks whether the cash-flow focus crowds out next-gen development.
findings.source: https://richardaboulafia.com/april-2024-letter ; https://news.bgov.com/esg/boeings-737-replacement-will-be-make-or-break-thomas-black ; https://fortune.com/2026/06/01/kelly-ortberg-boeing-innovation-aircraft/ (search excerpts only; full texts paywalled or blocked)
findings.use_in_model: The main outside support for a brand/talent premium. Opinion only, so log it as part of the H8 doctrine premium (suggested $0.5-2B, judgement) and show it as a slider, never as cash.
findings.quote: Boeing's ability to design and create new aircraft has atrophied across the board - civil and military

research.summary:
China and COMAC: what the evidence says, and how it could move the fps vs Do Nothing decision. (Label: china.)

1. China is large, but Boeing already runs its plans without it. In 2018 Chinese customers were 21.5% of Boeing Commercial Airplanes (BCA) revenue ($13.1B) and a third of 737 deliveries. By 2020 that had fallen to 7.9%, and in April 2025 China was about 10% of the commercial backlog. Boeing's 3 Nov 2026 China outlook forecasts 9,240 new aircraft for 2026-2045, of which 7,215 are single-aisle. That is about 21% of world demand. Boeing's revealed behaviour since 2022 is to plan without China and treat it as upside: Calhoun took China out of the $10B free-cash-flow target. When China stopped deliveries (the 2019-2024 MAX block and April-May 2025), Boeing waited, then remarketed or redirected the aircraft. It did not make concessions.

2. Washington's support is real but transactional. Boeing orders have been diplomatic currency in both directions: 300 aircraft in 2015, 300 in 2017, no large order for about nine years, then a 200-aircraft commitment at the May 2026 Trump-Xi summit. Ortberg says daily contact with the administration "up to POTUS" and calls the China order "100% dependent" on US-China relations. The same 2026 deal had the US promise China "strict supply guarantees" for aircraft engine parts. In other words, Washington traded COMAC's supply security for Boeing orders. US export controls on COMAC have been switched on and off as a bargaining tool: suspended May 2025, restored July 2025, capped October 2026. The July 2026 Section 232 proclamation and the Pentagon's 1260H military-company listing of COMAC show that the US treats commercial aerospace and COMAC as national-security matters. But I found no US official, report or think tank that links this to Boeing's 737 successor, or that offers money or rules to make Boeing launch one. ITIF (June 2026) wants allies to refuse to buy COMAC aircraft. CSIS (2020) and Aboulafia (testimony to the US-China Commission, 2025) argue against restricting COMAC.

3. COMAC is slow but backed by the state. C919 deliveries were about 13-15 in 2025 against a target of 75, and only 11 through September 2026. COMAC's plan is 200 a year by 2029. Its main constraints:
- It has no EASA or FAA approval before about 2028-31.
- It depends on LEAP-1C engines and US systems until the Chinese CJ-1000A engine arrives, around 2028-30.
- It has had $49-72B of state support (CSIS estimate), so it will persist whatever Boeing does.

The game's COMAC path matches IBA's analyst forecast for 2030 (93 a year) exactly. The 2026 figure (28) looks about twice too high. The long-run path (200 a year in 2045, 250 from 2050) is roughly 55% of Boeing's projected Chinese single-aisle demand, or about 15% of world single-aisle deliveries. That is more aggressive than Calhoun's own case of at most a 10% player by 2050, or Cirium's 5% fleet share by 2045.

4. The counter-evidence is strong. Boeing executives have called COMAC a distant third player since 2011 and have never cited it as a reason to launch an aircraft. In 2026, while COMAC flew its first international route, ITIF published its report and the Section 232 proclamation came out, Boeing's CFO said launch day "is not today, and it's not any time near".

How this could enter the model (my inference):
- (a) Treat Washington's support as order-flow upside that both options keep until the MAX ends. It is not a subsidy to the fps.
- (b) US curbs on COMAC have most value before about 2030, before the fps enters service, and policy keeps reversing them. So give them little weight.
- (c) China is moving towards Airbus (about 55% of China's fleet, a second Tianjin line, 160+ aircraft ordered in early 2026) and towards COMAC whatever Boeing does. Value the fps ex-China, as Boeing itself does.

Overall, the China and national-security element is real but belongs inside the Board's existing $2B doctrine-premium cap (H8). It is not a new source of value.

Access limits: WebFetch failed for every host tried (aerotime.aero, opb.org, sec.gov), and curl through the proxy reached none of the ten hosts tested. All web facts therefore come from WebSearch excerpts, rated medium or low. The search budget ran out before I could verify Boeing's claim of 150,000 US jobs tied to China, its 2000 lobbying for China's normal trade relations, and the exact wording of Faury's quotes. Note also that in B-1936 Calhoun's "40" is the 737 production rate per month, not a market share. On framing: the sources describe China as a strategic competitor and COMAC as a "Chinese military company" (Pentagon 1260H list), not as an enemy.

findings.topic: China's weight: revenue share
findings.claim: Before 2019 China was a fifth of Boeing's commercial revenue. Chinese customers paid $13.07B of BCA's $60.7B segment revenue in 2018 (21.5%), up from 16.5% (2016) and 18.9% (2017). The share fell to 15.7% in 2019 and 7.9% ($1.27B) in 2020. Company-wide, China was 13.6% of revenue in 2018 ($13.76B of $101.1B). From FY2021 the 10-K shows only 'Asia', not China.
findings.source: /home/user/aero-engine-gameboard/Boeing 10ks.zip -> Boeing 10ks.pdf: FY2018 10-K p.2604 and p.2606; FY2020 10-K p.1471-1472; FY2023 10-K p.405 and FY2024 10-K p.2285 (Asia only). Percentages are my calculation.
findings.quote: China 13,068 ... Total segment revenues $60,715 (BCA revenues by customer location, 2018)
findings.direction: neutral: China was a fifth of the business, but the share had collapsed to under 8% by 2020 for reasons Boeing did not control
findings.use_in_model: Bound the fps's China slice between about 10% (current backlog) and 21% (2018 peak) of narrowbody revenue. Do not use the outlook's 21% demand share as Boeing's share.

findings.topic: China's weight: deliveries
findings.claim: In 2015-2018 about one Boeing delivery in four, and one 737 in three, went to Chinese customers.
findings.source: Repo B-1537 (BofA conference, 21 Mar 2019, p.1076); B-1451 (Morgan Stanley, 12 Sep 2018, p.1172)
findings.quote: Over the last several years, 1 out of 4 airplanes we delivered went to a customer in China. 1 out of 3 737s went to Chinese customers.
findings.use_in_model: Before 2019 the 737 franchise depended on one state buyer for a third of its volume. Any fps case that assumes a pre-2019 China share carries single-government risk.

findings.topic: China's weight: backlog and how replaceable it is
findings.claim: By April 2025 China was about 10% of Boeing's commercial backlog, and Boeing kept its rate plan because other customers could absorb the aircraft. In May 2026 Ortberg said that if China's orders slipped, the slots and their deposits (pre-delivery payments) would go to other customers.
findings.source: Repo B-2292 (FQ1 2025 call, 23 Apr 2025, p.75); Transcript Digest (4).pdf p.65 (Bernstein conference, 27 May 2026)
findings.quote: Specifically on China, it represents approximately 10% of our commercial backlog. (B-2292) / if, for example, the China orders wouldn't happen by the end of the year, we probably would fill that with other PDPs. Those slots would go to someone else. (27 May 2026)
findings.direction: neutral: in the near term China demand can be replaced because the backlog is long
findings.use_in_model: China matters to the fps only in its 2035+ demand window. In near-term Do Nothing years, China orders can be replaced by other customers.

findings.topic: China's weight: 20-year demand forecast (Boeing's market outlook)
findings.claim: Boeing's 2026 China outlook (3 Nov 2026) projects 9,240 new aircraft for 2026-2045: 7,215 single-aisle (78%), 1,460 widebody, 405 regional and 160 freighters. The fleet grows from about 4,500 to over 9,800, and 42% of deliveries replace older aircraft. The 2026 global outlook (Jul 2026) projects 43,625 deliveries including 33,545 single-aisle, so China is about 21% of world deliveries and 21.5% of single-aisle (my calculation). Earlier editions: 8,830 (2024, of which 6,720 single-aisle) and about 9,000 (2025).
findings.source: boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-11-03-Boeing-Projects-Chinas-Commercial-Fleet-Will-More-than-Double-Over-20-Years; boeing.mediaroom.com 2026-07-17 global outlook release; China Daily 3 Nov 2026; Boeing 2024 China outlook release (26 Aug 2024). All from WebSearch extracts; pages could not be fetched.
findings.quote: Chinese carriers will take delivery of more than 7,200 single-aisle airplanes, representing 78% of the country's total projected deliveries (search extract)
findings.number: 9,240 total; 7,215 single-aisle; about 361 single-aisle a year on average
findings.direction: toward launch: the market is large. But this is demand, not Boeing orders.
findings.use_in_model: China single-aisle demand averages about 361 a year. Under Do Nothing after 2060, Boeing cedes about 21% of world single-aisle demand to Airbus and COMAC. Use it as the denominator for the COMAC path (see the COMAC forecast findings).

findings.topic: Executives on China's strategic value
findings.claim: Calhoun linked China access to Boeing's industry leadership. Losing it for too long would make Boeing 'pay a price', because China is about 25% of 10-year industry growth.
findings.source: Repo B-1806 (Bernstein conference, 3 Jun 2021, p.703); B-1907 (FQ2 2022 call, 27 Jul 2022, p.507)
findings.quote: Medium and long term, it does represent the difference between commercial aerospace leadership or not, given the size and scale of the China market.
findings.direction: toward launch: management itself frames China as decisive for leadership
findings.use_in_model: Supports a 'leadership' or doctrine premium. Weigh it against Boeing's actual behaviour (the ex-China planning finding), which went the other way.

findings.topic: Boeing behaviour: Zhoushan 737 completion centre
findings.claim: Boeing opened a 737 completion and delivery centre at Zhoushan in December 2018, during the trade war: first delivery to Air China on 15 Dec 2018, capacity 100 737s a year, Boeing's first such site outside the US. The completion centre is a joint venture with COMAC (Boeing majority, about $33M invested per Reuters); the delivery centre is wholly Boeing's. Muilenburg called it a win-win that also helped the Renton ramp. In June 2025 the first delivery after the tariff halt went through Zhoushan.
findings.source: Boeing press release 15 Dec 2018 (investors.boeing.com); Reuters via Investing.com; FlightGlobal (WebSearch extracts); repo B-1451 (12 Sep 2018, p.1172)
findings.quote: It's really a win-win as it adds jobs and capacity in China. And it's also helping us ramp up our U.S. production manufacturing in Renton. (B-1451)
findings.number: 100 aircraft a year capacity; about $33M stake
findings.direction: neutral: Boeing's China habit is to localise and partner, even with COMAC, to keep access, not to leave
findings.use_in_model: Past behaviour shows Boeing pays to stay in China rather than exit. Under Do Nothing the joint venture is a small stranded asset. The bigger signal is reputational: Boeing has never left a major market voluntarily.

findings.topic: Orders as bargaining chips: China buying around state visits
findings.claim: China placed its big Boeing orders through the state buyer CASC around state visits: 300 aircraft (about $38B list; 250 narrowbody, 50 widebody) during Xi's September 2015 US visit, and 300 aircraft (over $37B list; 260 737s, 40 777/787s) during Trump's November 2017 Beijing visit. The firm/commitment split was not disclosed.
findings.source: Repo B-1079 (FQ3 2015 call, 21 Oct 2015, p.1728); Boeing release 9 Nov 2017 (boeing.mediaroom.com) and AIN/Arab News (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: that included an announcement around 300 aircraft, 250 narrowbodies and 50 widebodies. (B-1079)
findings.direction: neutral: China treats Boeing orders as diplomatic currency, so they flow when relations are good and stop when they are not
findings.use_in_model: Model China demand for Boeing as lumpy, state-allocated tranches tied to the state of relations, not as a smooth market share.

findings.topic: Order freeze 2017-2026 and the 2026 reopening
findings.claim: After 2017 Boeing had no large Chinese order for about nine years. After the May 2026 Trump-Xi summit Ortberg said his 'primary objective was to reopen that market to our narrowbody airplanes'. The 200-aircraft commitment is being turned into firm orders airline by airline. By 16 Sep 2026 he stressed 'we didn't get an order for 200'.
findings.source: Transcript Digest (4).pdf p.54 (Bernstein, 27 May 2026); p.27 (Morgan Stanley, 16 Sep 2026)
findings.quote: we haven't had an order in nearly a decade. And we accomplished that, which is a major, major accomplishment ... They need well over 500 aircraft a year to support their GDP growth.
findings.number: 200 aircraft committed; about 9 years without an order; China needs over 500 a year
findings.direction: toward launch, weakly: China reopened to Boeing narrowbodies in 2026, so the market is not closed by default
findings.use_in_model: Keep a China slice in fps demand, but make it conditional on the state of US-China relations (Ortberg, Apr 2026: '100% dependent on the U.S.-China negotiations').

findings.topic: 2026 deal terms: US traded COMAC supply guarantees for Boeing orders
findings.claim: Trump announced the 200-aircraft commitment on 14 May 2026 and said it could reach 750. China's Commerce Ministry confirmed it on 20 May 2026, saying the US had committed to 'strict supply guarantees' for aircraft engine parts and components. These are the parts COMAC needs. Both sides would also seek reciprocal tariff cuts on at least $30B of goods each.
findings.source: CNBC 20 May 2026 (cnbc.com/2026/05/20/china-confirms-200-boeing-aircraft-order.html); RTHK 20 May 2026; Reuters via Yahoo Finance (WebSearch extracts; aerotime.aero and opb.org fetches blocked)
findings.quote: the US government committed to providing China with 'strict supply guarantees' for aircraft engine parts and components (search extract of MOFCOM statement)
findings.number: 200 committed; up to 750 claimed by Trump
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing on the 'DC will shield Boeing' argument: US policy sold Boeing jets and guaranteed COMAC's supply chain at the same time
findings.use_in_model: Do not assume US policy will choke COMAC to protect a Boeing successor. Washington uses COMAC's supply as a trade chip, so the 'restrictions raise Boeing demand' channel gets a low probability.

findings.topic: Revealed behaviour: Boeing plans ex-China
findings.claim: From 2022 Boeing removed China from its plans and targets: the November 2022 investor-day plan, the $10B 2025-26 free-cash-flow target, and the long-range framework 'always' ex-China. Calhoun also said a 50-50 share with Airbus was 'not an objective'. In B-1936 his '40 without China' is the 737 production rate per month, not a market share.
findings.source: Repo B-1971 (investor day, 2 Nov 2022, p.442); B-2052 (Bernstein, 2 Jun 2023, p.315); BX-1763 (West, 7 Sep 2023, p.285); B-1936 (p.448)
findings.quote: I've taken it out of all of our guidance, so our $10 billion in '25, '26 is -- has no China. (B-2052)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing: counter-evidence that political or strategic weight overrode the numbers. Boeing chose financial conservatism over market presence.
findings.use_in_model: Apply Boeing's own method: value the fps ex-China, with China as an upside sensitivity. That leaves the brief's $4-9B gap essentially unchanged.

findings.topic: Cost of China withholding orders
findings.claim: China's withholding of orders cost Boeing production. With no Chinese orders inside lead time, the 787 rate was cut from 14 to 12 (October 2019), then to 10 (January 2020). Boeing had reserved 777 and 787 slots for China. Calhoun held the 737 at rate 31 until China was clear. The 2022 MAX plan fell from about 500 to 387 deliveries, partly because China did not reopen.
findings.quote: The lack of orders from China in the past couple of years has put pressure on the production rate. (B-1596)
findings.number: 787: 14 to 12 to 10 a month; 737 plan about 500 to 387
findings.unit: aircraft per month; deliveries per year
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing for any case that counts on China: Chinese political risk is costly and recurring
findings.use_in_model: Add a China political-risk haircut, or a scenario of China going to zero for 3-5 years, to the fps's China demand.

findings.topic: 2019 grounding and the stranded China inventory
findings.claim: China was the first country to ground the MAX (March 2019) and resumed narrowbody MAX deliveries only in about January 2024, nearly five years later. Boeing held about 140 China-designated MAX at end-2022. It began remarketing in September 2022 and had placed 55 with others by July 2023 (85 left). About 40 remained at end-2024 and about 5 at 30 Sep 2025.
findings.source: Repo B-2008 (10-K FY2022, p.1538); B-2073 (FQ2 2023, p.297); B-2251 (10-K FY2024, p.2201); Boeing 10-Q Q3 2025 and MenTour Pilot / Star-Advertiser (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: approximately 140 aircraft in inventory that are designated for customers in China. We are remarketing some of these aircraft to other customers. (B-2008)
findings.direction: neutral: Boeing responded to China's block with patience, then commercial remarketing, not political concessions
findings.use_in_model: Revealed behaviour: when China closes, Boeing waits about 2-3 years and then redirects. That fits treating China as a replaceable upside, not a strategic must-have.

findings.topic: April-May 2025 delivery halt during the tariff war
findings.claim: On 15 Apr 2025, after China's 125% retaliatory tariffs, Beijing reportedly told airlines to stop taking Boeing jets and stop buying US aircraft parts. Jets waiting in China were flown back. Boeing had about 50 China deliveries in its 2025 plan, an exposure 'north of $1 billion', and said it would not build for customers who would not take aircraft. China lifted the ban around 12 May after the Geneva truce. Deliveries resumed on 9 Jun 2025, with 8 in June.
findings.source: Bloomberg 15 Apr 2025 (bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-04-15/...) and Reuters via The Star/Yahoo (WebSearch extracts); repo B-2293 (p.73), B-2288 (p.78), B-2294, B-2312 (29 May 2025, p.54)
findings.quote: we're not going to continue to build aircraft for customers who will not take them. (B-2294) / the Chinese airlines immediately said, I can't take delivery of the airplanes. And that's way more impactful to us. (B-2312)
findings.number: about 50 aircraft; over $1B; 8 delivered in June 2025
findings.direction: neutral leaning toward Do Nothing: China can switch off a US supplier within days, and Boeing answered by redirecting aircraft, not by pleading
findings.use_in_model: Size a China delivery-stop shock at about $1B per 50 aircraft for a year. It applies to both options while the MAX is built, and to the fps after 2035.

findings.topic: Lobbying and the DC relationship
findings.claim: Boeing is in constant contact with the White House on trade and benefits from aircraft orders built into trade deals. Ortberg said Boeing engages the administration daily, 'up to POTUS himself', that he wants tariff-free aircraft trade (as Airbus does), and that 'there's no better way to correct the balance of trade than to buy a large number of aircraft'. He added that many deal announcements are intentions, not contracts. In April 2026 he credited Trump with 'supporting us in international campaigns'.
findings.source: Repo B-2290 (FQ1 2025, 23 Apr 2025, p.76); B-2333 (Morgan Stanley, 11 Sep 2025, p.24); Transcript Digest (4).pdf p.84 (FQ1 2026 call, 22 Apr 2026). Muilenburg in August 2018 also said he had access to the administration on tariffs (CNN, WebSearch extract).
findings.quote: I don't think a day goes by where we aren't engaged with someone in the administration, including cabinet secretaries and up to POTUS himself. (B-2290)
findings.direction: toward launch, weakly: DC's support is real, but it sells existing products and is not tied to a new aircraft
findings.use_in_model: Model 'DC support' as order-flow upside that both options keep while Boeing builds narrowbodies (Do Nothing loses it only from 2045-60). It is not a subsidy to the fps's development cost.

findings.topic: Reliability of political purchase pledges
findings.claim: Peterson Institute (PIIE) data show China met only about 58% of its Phase One purchase targets in 2020, and about 52% for manufactured goods through November 2020. Aircraft lagged, with the MAX grounded and COVID cutting demand.
findings.source: GTR Review and SCMP reporting on PIIE tracker, 2021 (WebSearch extracts; PIIE page not fetched)
findings.quote: China fulfilled only 58 per cent of those targets in the deal's first year, 2020 (search extract)
findings.unit: % of Phase One purchase target met
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing: government-announced aircraft purchases are unreliable
findings.use_in_model: Discount politically announced Chinese orders (the 2026 '200, up to 750') by roughly 40-50% until they are firm (inference from the Phase One fulfilment rate).

findings.topic: China sanctions Boeing's defence unit
findings.claim: On 20 May 2024 China put Boeing Defense, Space & Security on its 'unreliable entity' list over Taiwan arms sales. The unit is barred from China-related trade and investment, and its executives from entering China. China had sanctioned the unit's CEO Ted Colbert in 2022. Reporting called the commercial effect symbolic.
findings.source: Bloomberg 20 May 2024 ('China Hits Boeing Defense, Two Others With Symbolic Sanctions'); AP via Boston Globe/Star Tribune (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: Boeing Defense, Space & Security will be added to Beijing's list of 'unreliable entities' (search extract)
findings.direction: neutral: Boeing is a lever China pulls in political disputes, whatever Boeing's product choices
findings.use_in_model: China's retaliation risk on Boeing's airliner business rises with US-China tension in both options. It does not differ between fps and Do Nothing.

findings.topic: COMAC: C919 deliveries against targets
findings.claim: C919 output keeps missing its targets. There were about 13 deliveries in 2024 and about 13-15 in 2025, against a 2025 target of 30, then 75, then 25. In 2026 there were 3 in Q1 and only 11 through September (Planespotters data), against 33 expected by the three big airlines and 25-28 forecast by IBA.
findings.source: Aviation Week 'C919 Deliveries Fall Short...' (2026); IBA 'COMAC Aircraft Programmes - Status & Outlook'; Leeham 15 Jan 2026; SCMP Apr 2026; Air Data News (Planespotters) Oct 2026 (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: only 11 C919s have been delivered to airlines through September 2026 (search extract, Air Data News)
findings.direction: toward launch, slightly: COMAC is slower than its plans, so less of the market goes to COMAC early on
findings.use_in_model: The game's 28 for 2026 is probably about twice the outturn (about 15-20 likely). Flag it, though the effect on 2030+ values is small.

findings.topic: COMAC: production plans and forecasts against the game path
findings.claim: At a March 2025 supplier conference COMAC set targets of 100 (2026), 150 (2027-28) and 200 a year by 2029. IBA's August 2026 forecast (analyst estimate) is about 28 (2026), 59 (2028) and 93 (2030), with the C919 fleet growing from 31 to 322 by 2030. The game's path (28/93/150/200/250 in 2026/30/35/45/50) matches IBA exactly to 2030. It reaches COMAC's 2029 target of 200 only in 2045, i.e. about 15 years of slippage. The game's 200 a year in 2045 is about 55% of Boeing's projected average Chinese single-aisle demand (361 a year). Cumulative COMAC output in 2026-2045 is about 2,700, roughly 38% of the 7,215 Chinese single-aisle deliveries (my calculation).
findings.source: Leeham 1 Sep 2026 'Boosting C919 Production Rates Remains Comac's Real Test'; Aircraft Interiors International / AJOT on IBA forecast (Aug 2026); SCMP / Aviation Week on 200 by 2029 (WebSearch extracts); /home/user/aero-engine-gameboard/wargame/dashgame/sd_options_phaseout.json (third_party.comac)
findings.quote: IBA's forecast of annual deliveries rising from about 28 in 2026 to 59 in 2028 and 93 by 2030 (search extract of Leeham)
findings.number: 93 a year in 2030 (IBA = game); COMAC target 200 a year by 2029
findings.direction: neutral: the game's COMAC path to 2030 sits on an analyst forecast; after 2030 it is a home-market-first stress case
findings.use_in_model: Keep IBA to 2030. Test the long run with a COMAC-slow case (Calhoun/Cirium) and a COMAC-on-plan case (200 by 2032). Under Do Nothing, a slower COMAC means Airbus, not Boeing, fills China.

findings.topic: COMAC: long-run share forecasts
findings.claim:
Long-run forecasts vary widely:
- Cirium: COMAC about 5% of the global fleet by 2045 (Airbus 47%, Boeing 39%).
- Calhoun (2023): 'even in an optimistic case, maybe in 2050, they get to be a 10% player'.
- Cirium via the FT: the C919 might take 20-30% of China's narrowbody market.
- One secondary report of an IBA 'aggressive scenario': 65% of new narrowbody deliveries to Chinese operators by 2030 (low confidence).
The game's 250 a year from 2050 is about 15% of world single-aisle deliveries (33,545/20 a year; my calculation).
findings.source: aviationa2z 19 Oct 2026 (Cirium, cited in /home/user/aero-engine-gameboard/wargame/reports/dash-2050-phaseout/data/franchise_research.json); repo BX-0380 (Bernstein, 2 Jun 2023, p.316); FT/Cirium and IBA via Simple Flying / residual-research (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: even in an optimistic case, maybe in 2050, they get to be a 10% player. (BX-0380)
findings.number: 5% fleet (2045, Cirium); at most 10% (2050, Calhoun); game about 15% of world single-aisle deliveries
findings.direction: neutral: the game is more aggressive on COMAC than Boeing's own CEO or Cirium
findings.use_in_model: Treat the game's COMAC path as a high case. A lower COMAC raises Airbus's take under Do Nothing, not Boeing's. It slightly raises fps volumes only if Boeing is still selling in China.

findings.topic: COMAC: certification outside China and export reach
findings.claim: The C919 holds only a Chinese (CAAC) type certificate, issued in September 2022, and has no EASA or FAA approval. EASA validation test flights began in Shanghai in November 2025, and by April 2026 were in the third of four phases. EASA's head said certification could take 3-6 years; IBA expects 2028-2031. The first scheduled international route, Air China Beijing-Ulaanbaatar, started on 12 Aug 2026 and replaced a 737 MAX 8.
findings.source: SCMP 'C919 stuck on tarmac in Europe...'; Aviation A2Z 13 Apr 2026; Aerospace Global News; Caixin 14 Aug 2026; Aviation A2Z 13 Aug 2026 (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: We should be certifying the C919 within three to six years (EASA executive director, search extract)
findings.direction: toward launch, slightly: COMAC cannot compete for Boeing's non-China customers before about 2030
findings.use_in_model: Supports the game's comac_first=1.0 (home market first) to about 2030. After EASA approval, allow COMAC exports to Asia, Africa and Latin America in a sensitivity.

findings.topic: COMAC: state funding
findings.claim: CSIS (Dec 2020) counted RMB328.5bn ($49bn) of identified state support for COMAC, and up to $72.1bn of potential support through 2020. The C919's ¥58bn development budget is estimated to have ended above ¥125bn (about $20bn). Shanghai has reportedly committed ¥70bn (about $9.7bn) to C919 supply chains. Separately, Yicai reported a $6.2B capital injection from state shareholders (year not confirmed).
findings.source: CSIS 'China's COMAC: An Aerospace Minor Leaguer' (Dec 2020), as recorded in /home/user/aero-engine-gameboard/wargame/reports/dash-2050-phaseout/data/franchise_research.json; ITIF Jun 2026 citing CSIS; Yicai; SCMP (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: RMB 328.5 billion (or $49 billion) (CSIS, via franchise_research.json)
findings.unit: USD of state support through 2020 (think-tank estimate)
findings.direction: neutral: COMAC persists whatever Boeing decides, so launching does not deter it and exit does not invite a new entrant that would not come anyway
findings.use_in_model: Do not credit the fps with 'deterring COMAC'. COMAC's path is set by the state and should be the same in both options.

findings.topic: COMAC: foreign content and domestic engine
findings.claim:
The C919 depends on Western, mainly US, systems:
- CFM LEAP-1C engines, with the GE-designed hot section.
- Honeywell: auxiliary power unit, wheels and brakes, flight controls.
- Collins: avionics, navigation and communications.
- Parker: fuel and hydraulics.
- Moog: high-lift system.
Bank of America counts 48 major US suppliers, 26 European and 14 Chinese. The domestic CJ-1000A engine targets Chinese certification in 2027. Analysts expect service in 2028-29 and mass production around 2030, and the maker has not applied to EASA or the FAA.
findings.source: Bank of America via SCMP/UNB; Aviation Week 'AECC Aiming To Certify C919 Engine In 2027'; OAG analyst Jan 2026 via Straits Times/Asia News Network (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: Chinese certification and initial deliveries of the CJ-1000A engine are likely to begin in 2027 or 2028, while mass production is expected from around 2030 (search extract)
findings.number: 48 US / 26 Europe / 14 China major suppliers; CJ-1000A mass production about 2030
findings.direction: neutral: US leverage over COMAC is strongest before about 2030, i.e. before an fps would enter service
findings.use_in_model: Any 'US restricts COMAC' benefit to Boeing falls mostly in 2026-2032, which suits the MAX more than the fps. Give the restriction channel little value in fps years.

findings.topic: US export controls on COMAC: on, off, on
findings.claim: In late May 2025 the Commerce Department suspended some export licences for COMAC (including GE's LEAP-1C for the C919 and CF34 for the C909), reportedly in response to China's curbs on critical minerals. It reversed this around 3-4 Jul 2025 as trade tensions eased. COMAC's 2025 output was disrupted by the June-July engine halt.
findings.source: New York Times via Yahoo/Bloomberg Law (28-29 May 2025); Reuters via ch-aviation / Ground News (3-4 Jul 2025) (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: the agency is reviewing exports of 'strategically significant' items destined for China (Commerce spokesperson, search extract)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing on the 'restrictions will protect Boeing' argument: controls are used as short-term bargaining chips and reversed
findings.use_in_model: Give a sustained US block on COMAC a low probability (inference from two reversals in 13 months). Its value to the fps should be small.

findings.topic: October 2026: US caps aircraft-parts licences for COMAC
findings.claim: Reuters (1 Oct 2026) reported that Commerce had slowed export licences for aircraft parts bound for China and capped what COMAC may receive, to stop it stockpiling, as leverage over China's rare-earth exports. The US-China truce was extended only to 10 Jan 2027.
findings.source: Asia Times Oct 2026 'For rare earth leverage, US caps aircraft parts licenses to China' (citing Reuters 1 Oct 2026); International Finance (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: limiting shipments to state-owned COMAC so it can't build up stockpiles (search extract relaying Reuters)
findings.direction: neutral: confirms US leverage over COMAC is real but is used for rare earths, not to protect Boeing's market
findings.use_in_model: Scenario input: COMAC slips 1-3 years if caps persist. This affects China's mix between Airbus and COMAC more than the fps business case.

findings.topic: US security framing: COMAC as a Chinese military company
findings.claim: On 6 Jan 2025 the Pentagon added COMAC to its Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies; the June 2026 update lists a COMAC entity (Shanghai Aircraft Design and Research Institute). In April 2023 Senators Rubio and Rick Scott asked Commerce to put COMAC on its military end-user list. In 2025 Rep. Krishnamoorthi (House Select Committee on the CCP) and Sen. Scott warned Ryanair against buying COMAC.
findings.source: Aviation Week 'Pentagon identifies COMAC as Chinese military contractor' (Jan 2025); Federal Register 2025-00070; WilmerHale alert 11 Jun 2026; rickscott.senate.gov 24 Apr 2023; democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: the Defense Department added Comac to a congressionally mandated list of Chinese military companies operating in the U.S. on Jan. 6 (search extract)
findings.direction: toward launch, weakly: Washington frames COMAC as a security issue and lobbies allies' airlines against it, which protects Western demand
findings.use_in_model: Supports keeping COMAC to its home market (comac_first) in the US-aligned world. It does not create a US payment or mandate for a Boeing successor.

findings.topic: Section 232: commercial aerospace declared a national-security industry
findings.claim: Commerce opened a Section 232 investigation into imports of commercial aircraft, jet engines and parts on 1 May 2025. A proclamation of 9 Jul 2026 found these imports 'threaten to impair' national security but imposed no tariffs. It directs Commerce and USTR to negotiate agreements, with updates due by 5 Jan 2027 and tariffs possible if talks fail within 180 days.
findings.source: White House fact sheet Jul 2026 (whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/07/...); KPMG, Thompson Hine, Expeditors alerts Jul 2026; Federal Register 9 May 2025 (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: commercial aircraft, jet engines, and their associated parts are being imported in quantities and under circumstances that threaten to impair U.S. national security (search extract)
findings.direction: toward launch, weakly: the US formally treats commercial aerospace as strategic. But the tool is import policy (aimed at Airbus and suppliers), and I found no link to Boeing's narrowbody plans.
findings.use_in_model: Evidence that a US exit from narrowbodies would collide with stated US policy, raising reputational and political cost under Do Nothing (inference). Value it inside the Board's $2B doctrine-premium cap (H8), not as extra cash.

findings.topic: Think-tank view: COMAC as a strategic threat (ITIF)
findings.claim: ITIF's June 2026 report calls COMAC a 'government-created, mercantilist-fueled national champion' that threatens market-based aviation. It urges a US-led pact of allies to refrain from buying Chinese commercial aircraft, and wants China in the OECD Aircraft Sector Understanding. It cites CSIS's $49-72B subsidy estimate and CrowdStrike on cyber theft.
findings.source: ITIF 15 Jun 2026 'COMAC: China's Looming Threat to the Global Aviation Industry' (itif.org/publications/2026/06/15/...); AviationNews.eu Jun 2026 (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: the rise of COMAC—China's government-created, mercantilist-fueled national champion—threatens the foundations of market-based commercial aviation (search extract)
findings.direction: toward launch, weakly: the policy community frames keeping a Western narrowbody supplier as strategic
findings.use_in_model: Qualitative support for a doctrine premium. The report does not mention Boeing's successor or propose funding it.

findings.topic: Counter-view: integration, not protection (CSIS, Aboulafia)
findings.claim: CSIS's Scott Kennedy (Dec 2020) called COMAC an 'aerospace minor leaguer' and argued that listing it as a military end-user and restricting US suppliers 'does not serve the American national interest'. Testifying to the US-China Commission in February 2025, Aboulafia urged the US to resist protectionism and stay integrated. He said the C919 is 'just enough behind' the A320neo and 737 MAX.
findings.source: CSIS blog 'China's COMAC: An Aerospace Minor Leaguer' (csis.org/blogs/trustee-china-hand/...); uscc.gov Richard_Aboulafia_Testimony.pdf (Feb 2025); The Star 8 Feb 2025 (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: listing COMAC as a military end-user and potentially restricting or banning U.S. firms to supply the C919 does not serve the American national interest (CSIS, search extract)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing, slightly: credible experts see COMAC as weak and the US gaining more from supplying it, which lowers the 'strategic urgency' argument
findings.use_in_model: Counterweight to the ITIF finding. Keep the doctrine premium modest and do not escalate it on COMAC grounds alone.

findings.topic: Boeing executives on COMAC, 2011-2026
findings.claim:
Boeing has consistently treated COMAC as a long-dated third player and never as a reason to launch:
- Albaugh (2011): 'The days of the duopoly are over'; the C919 'eventually ... they'll get it right'.
- McNerney (2012): 'at least a third competitor someday ... most likely Chinese'.
- Tinseth (2016): 'there will be a successful third competitor'.
- Calhoun (2021): 'plenty of growth ... to support 3 players'.
- Calhoun (2023): a 10% player by 2050 'should not intimidate us'.
- West (2023): 'We are comfortable with that.'
- A Boeing spokesperson (Feb 2024) called COMAC competition 'good for the industry'.
I found no Ortberg comment on COMAC in the 2026 transcripts. One French report (Oct 2026, low confidence) says he thinks airlines mainly want an improved 737 MAX.
findings.source: Repo BX-0021/BX-0022 (24 May 2011, p.2601); BX-0756 (15 May 2012, p.2344); Transcripts from 2006-2025_Compressed.pdf (Tinseth, 16 Mar 2016); BX-0280 (3 Jun 2021, p.713); BX-0380 (2 Jun 2023, p.316); BX-1744 (22 Mar 2023, p.370); CNBC 22 Feb 2024; Journal du Geek 19 Oct 2026 (WebSearch extracts)
findings.quote: the idea that we would have 3 competitors serving the global market should not intimidate us. It just shouldn't. (Calhoun, 2 Jun 2023)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing: Boeing's leaders have never used COMAC to justify a new aircraft
findings.use_in_model: A COMAC-driven 'must launch' argument has no support in Boeing's own record. Weight it low in the Board's tie rule.

findings.topic: Airbus's contrasting doctrine on COMAC
findings.claim: Airbus CEO Faury said in February 2025 that the market could become a 'triopoly'. In February 2026 (World Government Summit, Dubai) he called COMAC a serious long-term rival and said the best protection against an emerging competitor is to keep investing.
findings.source: Aero News Journal Feb 2025; Gulf News, WGS 2026 'Airbus CEO says Chinese plane maker Comac is no longer a distant rival' (WebSearch extracts; exact wording not verified because the search budget was exhausted)
findings.quote: the best way to be protected against an emerging competitor is to keep investing (search extract)
findings.direction: toward launch: the rival's doctrine is to out-invest COMAC
findings.use_in_model: Airbus players in the game may cite COMAC to justify investment. It is a signal for how Airbus responds, not new value for the fps.

findings.topic: China's market tilting to Airbus whatever Boeing does
findings.claim: Airbus's share of China's fleet rose from about 20% (2008) to over 50%, and about 55% by end-2025. Airbus opened a second A320 final assembly line in Tianjin in October 2025 (first delivery September 2026). In March 2026 China Eastern ordered 101 A320neo-family aircraft ($15.8B list, deliveries 2028-32) and Air China ordered 60 (about $9.5B). Chinese carriers had ordered 148 Airbus aircraft in 2025. Calhoun said China's 'objective is to keep it an even split'.
findings.source: Xinhua / People's Daily 22-23 Oct 2025; Caixin 26 Mar 2026; Aviation Week; Yicai; Exploring Tianjin Jan 2026 (WebSearch extracts); repo BX-0379 (2 Jun 2023, p.316)
findings.quote: as is often stated to us in all of our discussions around China is their objective is to keep it an even split. (BX-0379)
findings.number: about 55% Airbus fleet share; 101 + 60 A320neo ordered Mar 2026
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing for the China slice: China is being shared between Airbus (with local assembly) and COMAC regardless of Boeing's product
findings.use_in_model: Inference: if Boeing exits, China's 'even split' becomes Airbus against COMAC. The fps's China upside is capped by China's wish to balance and by Airbus's local assembly. Keep China small in the fps base case.

findings.topic: Boeing's own risk disclosure on China and COMAC
findings.claim: Boeing's FY2022-FY2024 10-Ks name only 'Airbus and entrants from China' as share-seeking competitors (Embraer and Bombardier were dropped in FY2018). They describe the US-China trade relationship as 'stalled as economic and national security concerns continue to be a challenge', and Chinese customers as 'a key component of our commercial aircraft backlog'.
findings.quote: Overall, the U.S.-China trade relationship remains stalled as economic and national security concerns continue to be a challenge. ... If we are unable to deliver aircraft to customers in China ... we may experience reduced deliveries and/or lower market share.
findings.use_in_model: Boeing formally treats COMAC as its only non-Airbus rival, and China as a political risk to disclose, not a market to count on.

findings.topic: Counter-evidence: no change to launch timing in 2026
findings.claim: 2026 brought COMAC's first international route, the ITIF report, the Section 232 finding and China's reopening. Despite all of it, Boeing's CFO said in March 2026 that a new programme day 'is not today, and it's not any time near', because none of the three conditions (market, technology, Boeing ready) are met. In July 2026 Ortberg said the next airplane is the chance to change industry profitability 'when the market is ready'. On 27 Oct 2026 he said 'nothing has changed on our outlook on new airplane'.
findings.source: Transcript Digest (4).pdf p.100 (conference, 17 Mar 2026, Malave); p.46 (FQ2 2026, 28 Jul 2026); p.16 (FQ3 2026, 27 Oct 2026)
findings.quote: I would say that there will be a day where we have to enter into a new program. That day is not today, and it's not any time near. (Malave, 17 Mar 2026)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing, or at least toward delay: geopolitical and COMAC pressure has not moved Boeing's timing
findings.use_in_model: Revealed preference: Boeing currently gives geopolitical pressure no weight in launch timing. Any 'subjective' premium the Board adds should stay within the H8 $2B cap.

findings.topic: Synthesis (my inference): how China and COMAC enter the fps decision
findings.claim:
Three channels, none of which closes a $4-9B gap.
- (a) US government support. It is demonstrated for selling existing jets (2015, 2017, 2025-26 deals), but it is transactional: in 2026 Washington guaranteed COMAC's parts to win Boeing orders. No source links it to funding or mandating a 737 successor. Value it as order-flow that both options keep until 2045-60.
- (b) US curbs on COMAC. They have been reversed twice in 13 months, and they matter most before the CJ-1000A arrives (about 2030), before an fps enters service. Value is low.
- (c) China closing to Boeing anyway. Boeing's backlog share is about 10%, Airbus has about 55% of China's fleet with two local lines, and COMAC is backed by the state and sells at home first. Boeing itself plans ex-China.
The main non-financial cost of Do Nothing is reputational and political: a US exit would hand China's 'second supplier' role to COMAC while US policy (Section 232, the 1260H list) calls aerospace strategic.
findings.source: Inference from the findings above (repo B-2052, B-2292, digest p.54/84/100; CNBC 20 May 2026; Section 232 fact sheet; IBA, CSIS and ITIF via WebSearch)
findings.unit: USD, suggested range for a China/national-security premium (inference)
findings.direction: toward launch only through the doctrine premium; the cash numbers stay toward Do Nothing
findings.use_in_model: Add a 'China and security' line inside the $2B doctrine premium (H8). Run sensitivities for: China at 0% / 10% / 20% of fps demand; COMAC at Calhoun-low vs the game path vs on-plan; and a US-restriction scenario limited to 2026-2032. Do not add a government subsidy to the fps: no evidence was found for one.

research.summary:
Scope and limits: I used the repo (Boeing evidence ids; the Boeing 10-K compilation and transcript PDFs; the Embraer transcript PDF, which despite its name runs to May 2026) and WebSearch. The shared web-search budget ran out partway through, and WebFetch was blocked for most hosts (govinfo, whitehouse, federalregister, heraldnet, airdatanews). Web facts below therefore come from search excerpts only. A few pre-2024 facts are from memory and are labelled as such.

What the evidence says:
(1) The Boeing-Embraer joint venture shows how Boeing behaves, not just what it says. Within about 3 months of Airbus taking the CSeries, Boeing went after Embraer for talent and capacity. The deal put an enterprise value of $5.26B on Embraer's commercial unit and paid $4.2B for 80%. Brazil let it pass its golden share (a government veto) only with conditions: jobs, headquarters and engineering stay in Brazil. Boeing borrowed $5.5B to fund the deal in the middle of the MAX grounding, then walked away on 25 Apr 2020 when cash was at risk. Walking away cost little: a $150M settlement in Sep 2024, about 3.6% of the price and below the $300-400M analysts expected. Boeing never mentioned Embraer again on calls (2020-2026), and the FY2024 10-K has no mention at all. Calhoun accepted leaving the 100-150 seat segment to Airbus and Embraer. This is the clearest counter-evidence: strategic and political weight did not outweigh liquidity.
(2) The framing needs correcting. Brazil is not a declared US enemy. It has been a Major Non-NATO Ally since 2019 (from memory, not re-checked). EO 14323 (30 Jul 2025) declared a national emergency over the Bolsonaro prosecution and speech cases, not over strategic rivalry. Even that order exempted civil aircraft and parts. Embraer paid only the 10% baseline tariff ($54M in 2025). Aircraft went back to zero tariff after the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026. Embraer is tied into the US and NATO: more than 40% US content, Pratt & Whitney GTF engines on the E2, about 2,500 direct US jobs plus 10,000 at suppliers (CEO figures), C-390 sales to at least six NATO states, and a Northrop KC-390 tanker team aimed at the USAF. In Boeing's own 10-Ks the list of competitors narrowed to 'Airbus and entrants from China' from the FY2022 10-K onward. The geopolitical cost of an exit therefore runs through COMAC, not Embraer.
(3) Embraer is an option, not a ready successor. In 2016 it said that if the incumbents 'give up a little bit of this market... we will look again'. The WSJ reported in 2024 that it had sounded out Saudi PIF and partners in Turkey, India and South Korea, and its CEO has said three or four makers could fit in the narrowbody market. But through May 2026 there is no decision and no timeline, and the company says it is focused on its existing products until 2030. Scale is the binding limit: 78 commercial deliveries in 2025, a target of 120 a year by about 2030, against 737 output of 47 a month (about 564 a year) in 2026. Embraer's commercial EBITDA margin was 2.7%, revenue $7.6B and free cash flow $491M.

How this could move the fps decision (my inferences):
(a) Do not add an 'enemy' premium for Brazil. If a doctrine premium (H8) is used, tie it to COMAC's share gain and to how DC reacts.
(b) The 'fps via Embraer' variant is not realistic as specified. Embraer funding 35% of capex means $21-23B, roughly 3 times its 2025 revenue. Unless the Brazilian state or a sovereign fund co-invests, cap Embraer's share or flag the variant. Any Embraer route also carries Brazilian conditions on jobs and IP, which shrink the US-jobs benefit of the programme.
(c) In the Do Nothing branch, add a small chance that an Embraer-led consortium enters 150-200 seats after about 2035. Most of the share Boeing gives up goes to Airbus and COMAC.
(d) On political weight: the tariff episode shows Washington carves aerospace out of trade fights when jobs and suppliers are argued. Embraer's roughly 12,500 US jobs (CEO figure) were enough to win an exemption within about 3 weeks. That supports a non-zero 'DC pressure' term against exit. But Boeing's 2020 Embraer exit and the cheap settlement show that pressure has not held Boeing to a commitment once its cash was threatened.

findings.topic: Boeing-Embraer JV rationale
findings.claim: Boeing sought Embraer about 3 months after Airbus took control of the CSeries (Oct 2017). It sought the deal explicitly for engineering talent and manufacturing capacity, and to gain a sub-737 product (E2), rather than concede the 100-150 seat segment.
findings.quote: it also gives us more resources and, I'll say, an engineering talent set that's complementary to Boeing's (B-1420); they also bring to us additional engineering capacity and manufacturing capacity (B-1567)
findings.unit: months from Airbus-CSeries deal to Embraer talks
findings.direction: toward launch (Boeing's instinct is to buy capacity rather than concede a segment)
findings.use_in_model: Precedent for an inorganic or partner response to Airbus consolidation; supports keeping the 'fps via Embraer' variant and giving Boeing a reaction probability to rival moves.

findings.topic: JV price and structure
findings.claim: The Commercial Aviation JV valued 100% of Embraer's commercial unit at $5.263B enterprise value. Boeing would pay $4.2B for 80%, up from $3.8B at the July 2018 MoU. Boeing would also take 49% of a C-390 JV. Embraer kept a put option on its 20% at the deal price plus inflation for a 10-year lock-up.
findings.source: Embraer Special Call 17 Dec 2018 (Embraer Transcripts PDF p561, p564); Boeing 10-K FY2018 (Boeing 10ks.pdf p2557, B-1492); 10-K FY2019 p542 (B-1646)
findings.quote: The price went up from $4.75 billion to $5.263 billion. That's the enterprise value for 100%... 80% of that now is $4,200,000,000. Before, it was $3,800,000,000
findings.unit: USD bn (EV 100%; 80% price Dec 2018; 80% price Jul 2018)
findings.use_in_model: Calibrates what Embraer's whole commercial engineering and production base cost: about $5.3B, or 8-9% of the $60-65B fps. Useful for pricing a talent and capacity acquisition or a JV entry ticket.

findings.topic: Brazilian golden share and political conditions
findings.claim: Brazil's government reviewed the deal under its golden share on 10 Jan 2019 and chose not to veto. The deal was conditioned on headquarters, operations and management staying in Brazil, and press reports say on current Brazilian job levels and engineering capabilities being kept. Defence and business jets stayed with Embraer.
findings.source: Boeing 10-K FY2018 (p2557); Embraer Special Call 17 Dec 2018 p561-562; Embraer FQ4 2018 call 14 Mar 2019 p547; engineeringnews.co.za 11 Jan 2019 https://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/embraer-boeing-deal-gets-approval-from-the-new-brazilian-government-2019-01-11 (search excerpt)
findings.quote: the Government of Brazil reviewed the terms of the strategic partnership and advised it would not exercise its Golden Share veto power (10-K); Headquarters, operations and management will remain in and be committed to development in Brazil (Embraer)
findings.unit: % of Embraer shareholder votes in favour (26 Feb 2019)
findings.use_in_model: Any fps-via-Embraer variant should carry Brazilian political conditions (work share and IP kept in Brazil). That reduces the US-jobs and brand benefit a 'DC pressure' premium would credit to the fps.

findings.topic: Boeing accommodated a foreign government
findings.claim: Boeing publicly deferred to Brazilian government concerns and reshaped the deal (carving out defence) to win approval, showing it will trade structure for political consent.
findings.source: Repo B-1351 (Greg Smith, Cowen, 7 Feb 2018, Transcripts p1311); Boeing FQ4 2017 call 31 Jan 2018 p1332
findings.quote: being very mindful and being very respectful to the Brazilian government's priorities and needs as well as Embraer's (Smith); We know that the government of Brazil has raised some concerns or issues that we fully respect (Muilenburg)
findings.use_in_model: Boeing responds to government constraints by restructuring, not by abandoning; relevant to how it would respond to DC pressure over an exit.

findings.topic: Boeing levered up for the JV mid-crisis
findings.claim: During the MAX grounding Boeing raised $5.5B of debt in Q3 2019, mainly to pre-fund the Embraer purchase. It stayed committed until cash ran out.
findings.quote: We raised additional debt in the quarter, increasing the balance by $5.5 billion, primarily to fund the Embraer acquisition
findings.direction: toward launch (strategic commitment survives moderate stress)
findings.use_in_model: A strategic premium held through one crisis (the grounding) but not two (grounding plus COVID). Condition any doctrine premium on the state of the balance sheet.

findings.topic: Termination of the JV (counter-evidence)
findings.claim: On Saturday 25 Apr 2020 Boeing terminated both JVs, citing unsatisfied closing conditions, after 2 years of work. It acted amid the MAX grounding and COVID, despite the Brazilian political fallout and reputational cost.
findings.source: Repo B-1674 / BX-0216 (Calhoun, FQ1 2020 call, 29 Apr 2020, Transcripts p859); 10-K FY2020 p1470 (B-1792)
findings.quote: We worked diligently for 2 years to finalize the transaction, but ultimately, we could not come to resolution around critical, unsatisfied conditions... continued negotiation was no longer helpful.
findings.use_in_model: The strongest precedent that strategic, political and brand weight did NOT override cash preservation. Cap or zero the H8 doctrine premium in liquidity-stress states.

findings.topic: Embraer's side of the break-up
findings.claim: Embraer called the termination wrongful and launched arbitration. It bore separation costs ($21.8M in Q1 2020 vs $12.3M in Q1 2019) and arbitration and integration costs of about $17M a quarter, roughly 1.5pp of margin, in 2021-22.
findings.source: Embraer FQ1 2020 call 1 Jun 2020 (Embraer Transcripts p469, p471); FQ4 2021 call 10 Mar 2022 p351; FQ1 2022 call 28 Apr 2022 p336
findings.quote: Embraer has been in compliance with all of the conditions under the agreement, and we will work in the arbitration process to pursue any and all remedies available to compensate Embraer for the wrongful termination
findings.unit: USD m separation cost Q1 2020 / USD m per quarter arbitration and integration / pp margin
findings.use_in_model: Shows the partner bears most of the cost of a failed tie-up. Lowers Embraer's appetite for a repeat JV and should raise the JV variant's execution-risk haircut.

findings.topic: Arbitration outcome and damages
findings.claim: In Sep 2024 the arbitration ended with Boeing paying Embraer $150M gross under a 'collar agreement'. Analysts had expected $300-400M, and BofA said it covered only about half of the roughly $300M in termination costs management had estimated. Embraer shares fell about 5%. Embraer booked the $150M in Q3 2024, adding about 900bp to that quarter's margins.
findings.source: FlightGlobal Sep 2024 https://flightglobal.com/airframers/boeing-to-pay-embraer-150-million-to-settle-dispute-over-failed-acquisition/159984.article ; ch-aviation 144833; TipRanks/BofA (search excerpts, 16 Sep 2024); Embraer FQ3 2024 call 8 Nov 2024 p190
findings.quote: there was an important $150 million contribution from the Boeing agreement, which propped up both margin by circa 900 basis points for the period (Embraer)
findings.use_in_model: Walking away from a $4.2B strategic commitment cost about $150M, roughly 0.25% of a $60B fps (my inference). Monetary penalties for abandoning partner or strategic commitments are small; reputational ones did not show up in money.

findings.topic: Boeing's silence after exit
findings.claim: After 29 Apr 2020 Boeing did not mention Embraer on any earnings call or conference in the transcript set through 2025, apart from one executive bio, nor in the 2026 calls. The FY2024 10-K has zero Embraer mentions, against an arbitration note in the FY2023 10-K (p404).
findings.source: My count: grep of 'Transcripts from 2006-2025_Compressed.pdf' (last substantive mention p859/869, Apr 2020), 'Transcript Digest (4).pdf' (2026 calls: 0), Boeing 10ks.pdf FY2024 section (0) vs FY2023 (B-2131 p404)
findings.unit: Embraer mentions in Boeing calls May 2020-Oct 2026
findings.use_in_model: No sign that brand or political cost from the failed tie-up forced Boeing back to Brazil. My inference: the reputational term for the 2020 exit was close to zero.

findings.topic: Conceding the 100-150 seat segment (counter-evidence)
findings.claim: After the JV collapsed and the NMA was shelved, Calhoun accepted leaving the small-narrowbody segment to the A220 and E2 with no Boeing product. The segment has stayed uncontested by Boeing since 2020.
findings.source: Repo B-1666 / BX-0220 (FQ1 2020 call, 29 Apr 2020, Transcripts p869); B-1686
findings.quote: Embraer's not going away. They're going to fight tooth and nail to win at that low end of the marketplace, and they'll battle Airbus, the former Bombardier, in doing so. And I don't think that's going to move the market in any significant way
findings.use_in_model: Precedent that Boeing will vacate a segment to foreign rivals without visible DC backlash. The segment is small compared with the 737's, so scale the precedent down.

findings.topic: Embraer's stated reaction function
findings.claim: Embraer said it would not launch anything larger than the E2 while Boeing and Airbus stay in the segment, but would 'look again' if they vacate. In 2011 it had explicitly ruled out going head-to-head with the A320 and 737-800.
findings.source: Embraer FQ3 2016 call 31 Oct 2016, Paulo Cesar de Souza e Silva, CEO (Embraer Transcripts p695); FQ2 2011 call 29 Jul 2011 p1055
findings.quote: I don't think that we'll launch any new aircraft that will be larger than the E2, if Boeing and Airbus are still in this segment... if they decide to... give up a little bit of this market, yes, at that moment, it's different. So we will look again.
findings.use_in_model: In the Do Nothing branch, add a conditional probability that Embraer (with partners) enters 150-200 seats once a Boeing exit is credible. The entrant gains part of the vacated share.

findings.topic: Embraer 737-sized jet reports (2024)
findings.claim: WSJ reported (around 30 Apr 2024) that Embraer was exploring a new narrowbody to rival the 737 and A320 successors. It said Embraer had sounded out Saudi Arabia's PIF and manufacturers in Turkey, India and South Korea as partners and backers. Embraer said it had the capability but no plans for a sizable new project.
findings.source: WSJ via tovima.com https://tovima.com/wsj/brazils-embraer-plots-a-new-737-sized-jet-to-rival-boeing ; aviationa2z 2 May 2024 https://aviationa2z.com/index.php/2024/05/02/embraer-no-plans-to-make-new-aircraft/ (search excerpts)
findings.quote: the company certainly has the capability to develop a new narrow-body aircraft (Embraer spokesman, per excerpt)
findings.unit: USD bn development cost (single Economist-via-Metropoles excerpt; unconfirmed)
findings.direction: toward launch (a non-US consortium could fill a vacuum)
findings.use_in_model: Potential entrant partners are multi-aligned states (Saudi, Turkey, India, Korea), not US adversaries. Model an entrant consortium in the Do Nothing branch after about 2035.

findings.topic: Embraer CEO on room for more makers; Airbus pushback
findings.claim: Gomes Neto told the FT the narrowbody market could support 'three or four' major manufacturers in coming decades, against about 40,000 aircraft of demand over 20 years. He said a move was unlikely before the next decade. Airbus CEO Faury said Embraer should 'think twice' before entering against Airbus, Boeing and COMAC.
findings.source: airdatanews https://www.airdatanews.com/embraer-ceo-says-global-jet-market-has-room-for-more-boeing-and-airbus-rivals ; infomoney https://www.infomoney.com.br/?p=3059855 ; airdatanews Faury piece (search excerpts; dates not confirmed, likely late 2024)
findings.quote: three or four
findings.use_in_model: Supports a non-zero long-run entrant term. The incumbent (Airbus) signals it would fight entry hard.

findings.topic: Embraer 2025-26: studies, no decision
findings.claim: Through May 2026 Embraer repeatedly said customers ask it to 'go bigger'. It said it is studying new commercial or business jets, investing in wings, fuselage and cockpit technology and talking to engine suppliers, but has no decision or timeline and will focus on its existing products to 2030.
findings.source: Embraer FQ4 2024 call 27 Feb 2025 p128; FQ1 2025 call 6 May 2025 p105; FQ3 2025 call 4 Nov 2025 p70; FQ1 2026 call 8 May 2026 p13 (Embraer Transcripts PDF)
findings.quote: customers, they have asked us about our plans to go bigger... We don't have a decision (May 2025); until 2030, we have -- we will focus a lot on the products we have (Feb 2025); we are making studies for a new cycle of products (May 2026)
findings.use_in_model: Put any Embraer entry in the 2030s, not before. It does not threaten the fps's 2030-2040 window, but it could occupy the post-2045 MAX phase-out gap.

findings.topic: Embraer scale vs a 737 exit
findings.claim: Embraer delivered 78 commercial jets in 2025 and targets 120 a year by the end of the decade. Boeing's 737 was at 47 a month (about 564 a year) in Jul 2026, heading to 52. Embraer's planned 2030 commercial output is therefore about 21% of the 737's 2026 annual rate (my calculation).
findings.source: Embraer FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p41; FQ1 2026 call 8 May 2026 p11; Boeing FQ2 2026 call 28 Jul 2026 (Transcript Digest (4) p37, p41)
findings.quote: by the end of the decade, we expect to reach production of 120 commercial jets and 200 executive jets and 10 KC-390 (Embraer); On 737, we're now ramping to 47 airplanes per month (Boeing)
findings.unit: Embraer 2025 commercial deliveries / Embraer target per year / 737 per year at rate 47
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing relative to the 'ceding to Brazil' framing
findings.use_in_model: In Do Nothing, give the vacated 737 share mostly to Airbus and COMAC; Embraer is a marginal taker. Geopolitical cost should be attached to COMAC's gain.

findings.topic: Embraer financial capacity for a JV share
findings.claim: Embraer 2025: revenue $7.6B, adjusted EBIT $657M, adjusted free cash flow $491M, Commercial Aviation adjusted EBITDA margin 2.7%. Net debt ex-Eve was $111M at end-2024. The war game's 'fps via Embraer' (Embraer pays 35% of capex) implies $21-23B, about 3 times Embraer's annual revenue and about 45 times its 2025 free cash flow (my calculation).
findings.source: Embraer FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p41-42; FQ4 2024 call 27 Feb 2025 p119; repo /home/user/aero-engine-gameboard/wargame/profiles/boeing/objectives.md (fps via Embraer terms)
findings.quote: In Commercial Aviation, revenues increased by 7%... The adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 2.5% to 2.7%
findings.unit: USD bn revenue / USD bn FCF / % commercial EBITDA margin (2025)
findings.direction: neutral (undermines the JV variant as specified)
findings.use_in_model: Cap Embraer's capex share at about 5-10% unless BNDES or a sovereign fund co-funds, or flag the 35% JV variant as infeasible without a Brazilian state backstop.

findings.topic: E2 momentum in the segment Boeing vacated
findings.claim: Embraer sold almost 200 E2s in 2025 (157 firm E2 orders plus 140 options in 12 months to Q4 2025). It has 24 E2 operators and a commercial backlog of $14.5-15B, a record. The vacated 100-146 seat segment was filled by rivals.
findings.source: Embraer FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p41; FQ1 2026 call 8 May 2026 p4, p15
findings.quote: Remember, we sold the last year, I mean, almost 200 E2s
findings.unit: E2s sold in 2025 / USD bn commercial backlog Q1 2026
findings.use_in_model: Evidence that an exited segment gets captured by rivals within about 5 years. It supports the share-loss assumption in Do Nothing.

findings.topic: Embraer US footprint and US content
findings.claim: Embraer CEO: about 2,500 direct US employees plus 10,000 supplier jobs, 12,500 in all. More than 40% US content per aircraft, and the E2 uses Pratt & Whitney GTF engines. Melbourne, Florida campus of about 543,485 sq ft (FY2025 20-F). A company brochure cites more than $21B of planned US supplier purchases over 5 years across 250+ companies.
findings.source: Gomes Neto via defesanet https://www.defesanet.com.br/?p=1075346 and Reuters/intellinews (Jul 2025, search excerpts); Embraer FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p48; Embraer 20-F FY2025 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1355444/000162828026021824/erj-20251231.htm (search excerpt); Embraer USA brochure https://www.embraer.com/media/betmhabc/folder-usa-single-pages.pdf (undated); Finnair call 23 Mar 2026 p26 (PW1900G)
findings.quote: we'll keep buying a lot of U.S. parts because more than 40% of our aircraft has a U.S. content (Gomes Neto, Mar 2026)
findings.unit: US jobs supported / % US content / USD bn planned US purchases over 5 yrs
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing relative to the 'enemy' framing
findings.use_in_model: Share Boeing loses to Embraer partly stays in the US supply base (engines, avionics). Do not count it as a full loss to an adversary.

findings.topic: 2025 tariffs: aircraft exempted after lobbying
findings.claim: EO 14323 (30 Jul 2025, effective 6 Aug) added a 40% duty on Brazil (50% in total) but exempted civil aircraft, engines and parts (Annex I). The 10% baseline remained. Embraer had warned the full tariff meant about $9M extra per aircraft and a pandemic-like hit. It and US airlines lobbied, arguing the E175 has no substitute under US scope clauses, and the exemption came about 3 weeks after the threat.
findings.source: EO 14323 via presidency.ucsb.edu https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/node/378230 and Federal Register 2025-14896 (5 Aug 2025); ch-aviation 156634 https://www.ch-aviation.com/news/156634-united-states-backs-down-on-additional-embraer-tariffs ; intellinews/Reuters ($9M); Embraer FQ2 2025 call 5 Aug 2025 p82, p91
findings.quote: we are happy that we were able to come from 50% to 10%... we compiled this information and we took it to the right people who had to see it (Gomes Neto)
findings.unit: % tariff faced / USD m extra cost per aircraft avoided
findings.direction: toward launch (DC protects aerospace jobs and supply chains)
findings.use_in_model: Evidence for a real 'DC pressure' term. If about 12,500 US jobs won a carve-out for a foreign OEM, Boeing's far larger footprint would draw stronger pushback against an exit (my inference). Size it from jobs, not from 'enemy' rhetoric.

findings.topic: Tariff costs actually paid by Embraer
findings.claim: Embraer paid $54M in US tariffs in 2025 ($27M in Q4 2025). It took another $13M in Q1 2026, mainly an inventory effect, and expected $11M more in Q2 2026. It said it was the only aircraft maker paying US tariffs, because EU, UK and Japan deals had restored zero tariffs on aircraft.
findings.source: Embraer FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p42, p46, p48; FQ1 2026 call 8 May 2026 p12
findings.quote: last year, we paid $54 million in tariffs (Paiva); Embraer was the only manufacturer to pay tariffs on aircraft exports before (Gomes Neto)
findings.use_in_model: US trade policy consistently zeroes aircraft tariffs with allies, protecting Boeing's export base. That is a structural DC interest in a US civil-aircraft franchise.

findings.topic: Correcting the 'declared US enemy' framing for Brazil
findings.claim: The 2025 US action against Brazil was a national-emergency tariff over Brazil's prosecution of Bolsonaro and speech rulings affecting US persons, not a strategic-adversary designation. Brazil was designated a Major Non-NATO Ally in 2019 (from memory, not re-checked this session). EO 14361 (20 Nov 2025) narrowed the tariff citing negotiation progress after Lula and Trump met in Kuala Lumpur in Oct 2025.
findings.source: EO 14323 text via presidency.ucsb.edu and ballotpedia (search excerpts); EO 14361 (20 Nov 2025) via statutes.vaquill.ai (search excerpt); Embraer FQ3 2025 call 4 Nov 2025 p69; MNNA from memory
findings.quote: the policies, practices, and actions of the Government of Brazil... constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat (EO 14323, per excerpt); President Lula met with President Trump in Kuala Lumpur a week ago (Embraer)
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing (removes a Brazil 'enemy' premium)
findings.use_in_model: Do not apply an adversary premium to Brazil or Embraer gains. Reserve any geopolitical premium for COMAC, the official 'pacing challenge'.

findings.topic: Feb 2026: IEEPA struck down; aircraft back to zero
findings.claim: On 20 Feb 2026 the Supreme Court held 6-3 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs, which voided the Brazil 40% duty. The replacement Section 122 10% surcharge (from 24 Feb 2026) exempted civil aircraft, engines and parts under the 1979 Agreement on Trade in Civil Aircraft, and Embraer confirmed a zero tariff. Later reports (single sources, lower confidence) say the Court of International Trade invalidated Section 122 on 7 May 2026 and that a Brazil Section 301 action at 25% from 22 Jul 2026 also exempts civil aircraft parts.
findings.source: Holland & Knight Mar 2026 https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/03/supreme-court-ieepa-ruling-and-new-us-tariffs-implications-for-civil ; Global Trade Alert https://globaltradealert.org/blog/from-ieepa-to-section-122 ; Ward and Smith (CIT); Embraer FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p48 (search excerpts plus repo)
findings.quote: we confirm that all Embraer aircraft engines and parts are exempt from the 10% tariffs as of February (Gomes Neto)
findings.unit: % US tariff on Brazilian civil aircraft from Feb 2026
findings.use_in_model: Across every 2025-26 tariff regime civil aerospace was carved out. Treat US policy as committed to an open civil-aircraft trade regime that favours the US incumbent.

findings.topic: Embraer defence ties to NATO and the US
findings.claim: C-390 customers include NATO members Portugal, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, the Czech Republic and Sweden, plus Greece (2026), as well as South Korea and the UAE (10 firm plus 10 options, May 2026, the second-biggest order after Brazil's). In 2024 Embraer sold 14 C-390s and 12 A-29s. In Feb 2026 it signed an MoU with Northrop Grumman to pitch a KC-390 tanker for the USAF NGAS, after an L3Harris tie-up ended in 2024. It builds A-29s in Jacksonville and has sold them to USAF Special Operations Command.
findings.source: Embraer FQ4 2024 call 27 Feb 2025 p156; FQ1 2026 call 8 May 2026 p4; FQ1 2020 call p470; FQ2 2023 call p275; Breaking Defense Feb 2026 https://breakingdefense.com/2026/02/northrop-brazils-embraer-partner-on-kc-390-to-pitch-us-others/ ; Wikipedia C-390 orders list (search excerpt; order statuses vary by source)
findings.quote: shout out to the UAE, who just signed a purchase agreement for 10 C-390 aircraft plus 10 options, the second biggest order after the Brazilian Air Force
findings.unit: C-390 sold in 2024 / A-29 sold in 2024 / UAE C-390 firm+options
findings.direction: toward Do Nothing relative to the 'enemy' framing
findings.use_in_model: Embraer is Western- and NATO-aligned. Share it gains is not share for a US adversary.

findings.topic: Embraer partners in multi-aligned states
findings.claim: Embraer is building partnerships in India (with Mahindra on the C-390 for the Indian Air Force MTA, needing 50% local origination; an Adani MoU on E175 civil production), Turkey (an Apr 2025 MoU to co-develop parts and expand E2 capacity) and Saudi Arabia (a 2024 MoU on production, assembly and maintenance).
findings.source: Embraer FQ3 2025 call 4 Nov 2025 p69; FQ4 2025 call 6 Mar 2026 p40, p52; FQ1 2025 call 6 May 2025 p111; Saudi MoU per search excerpt (eplaneai/aviacionline)
findings.quote: Our intention is to expand our production capacity of E2 aircraft and Turkey has a highly developed aeronautical industry (Gomes Neto, May 2025)
findings.unit: % local content required in India C-390 bid
findings.use_in_model: A Boeing exit would push any Embraer-led entrant toward Saudi, Turkish and Indian capital and work share, diluting US industrial leadership rather than handing share to an adversary.

findings.topic: Brazilian state backing for Embraer
findings.claim: In Feb 2025 the Lula government and Embraer announced R$20B of investment in Brazil to 2030 under 'Nova Indústria Brasil'. On the same day BNDES approved R$2.1B of financing for 16 jets for Republic Airways. In 2020 Embraer raised more than $1B from BNDES, US EXIM and banks.
